articles.title: Apps to distract you from the endless cycle of doomscrolling | TechCrunch
articles.text:
You open your phone to check the time or a quick message. The next thing you know, an hour has passed and you’ve scrolled through endless celebrity drama, cat videos, awful news stories, influencer rants, and whatever else the algorithm decided to throw at you.
Even though you probably don’t want to keep wasting your time and energy on this mind-numbing content, you do it again the next day.
Doomscrolling, the habit of spending excessive amounts of time consuming content on social media, has become incredibly widespread. A survey from last year found that 64% of Americans say they doomscroll.
Researchers have warned that doomscrolling can negatively affect several aspects of your well-being, including your mental health and attention span. Spending long periods scrolling can lead to brain fatigue, difficulty focusing, and disrupted sleep. And if a lot of the content you’re consuming is negative or stressful, it can leave you feeling disheartened, anxious, and emotionally drained.
It’s hard to break the cycle of doomscrolling, but there are plenty of apps that provide content that’s engaging and productive.
Of course, you could always read a book or go for a walk (we have a guide on how to stop doomscrolling), but this list is for when you have a few spare minutes and want something to do on your phone that isn’t endless scrolling.
Finch
Finch is a self-care pet app that’s designed to help you build healthy habits. You care for a cute virtual pet by completing small daily goals, such as drinking enough water, going on a walk, and practicing mindfulness. You can write about your day, complete a breathing exercise, or send good vibes to a friend by adding them to the app.
The more self-care you do, the more your pet thrives. The app offers a fun way to trade mindless scrolling for small moments of self-care.
Finch is available for free on iOS and Android.
Libby
Libby is a free reading app that connects you to your local public library’s digital collection of ebooks, audiobooks, and magazines. All you need is a library card to borrow thousands of titles, which makes it easy to turn screen time into something productive.
You can explore a new book during a commute or while waiting at a doctor’s office, turning moments when your fingers might otherwise itch to scroll into opportunities to read.
Libby is available for free on iOS and Android.
Dudel Draw
If you want to take a break from doomscrolling and try something creative, Dudel Draw might be a good app for you. Each day, the app gives you a random shape that you turn into a drawing. These daily shapes vary from basic geometrical forms to more complex and abstract designs.
You can also get your friends in on the creativity with some fun competition by comparing your different creations, which could provide a nice break from sending each other endless TikToks or Instagram Reels.
Dudel Draw is available for free on iOS.
Radio Garden
If you still want to feel connected to the world without scrolling through social media, you can check out Radio Garden. The app lets you listen to over 25,000 live radio stations from across the globe.
Once you open the app, you’ll see green dots marking cities and towns. Tap any dot to listen to radio stations broadcasting from that location. You can add favorites or search for radio stations, countries, and places.
Radio Garden is free, but it also offers an ad-free premium plan for $2.99 per month. The app is available on both iOS and Android.
Elevate
Elevate is an app designed to help improve focus, memory, reading, math skills, and other cognitive abilities. It includes over 40 games to train different abilities you use in everyday life, from reading faster to comparing prices more efficiently.
You can track training streaks and compare your mind’s performance over time.
The app offers a free version with access to three games per day, or a yearly subscription of $39.99 for unlimited access. It’s available on both iOS and Android.
Vocabulary
Vocabulary is an app that helps you learn new words every day. You can pick your difficulty level and choose categories that interest you, like emotions, the human body, business, and more. Each word comes with a definition, example sentences, and a guide on how to pronounce it.
The app also includes mini-games to help you review the words you’ve learned. You can set a goal of how many words you want to learn each week and create a regular learning routine.
Vocabulary offers a free trial, and then costs $4.99 per month or $59.99 per year. It’s available on iOS and Android.
Seterra
If you’re a geography nerd looking to test your knowledge or just want to improve your geography skills, Seterra is perfect for you. The app features over 300 different games to test your map skills. You can test your knowledge of world flags; discover oceans, seas, and rivers; and explore mountain ranges and volcanoes across the globe.
Seterra lets you track your progress across categories and see leaderboards for top scorers for each game.
The app is free and available on both iOS and Android.
NYT Games
The NYT Games app offers several word, logic, and number games that change every day to exercise your mind. You can play the crossword, try the word-guessing game Wordle, group words with a common theme in Connections, see how many words you can make from seven letters in Spelling Bee, and more.
The app costs $5.99 per month for unlimited access and archives, but some games like Wordle, Strands, and the Mini Crossword are available to play for free.
NYT Games is available on both iOS and Android.
Drops
If you want to learn a new language but want to try something other than Duolingo, Drops is a good option. The app uses visually engaging mini‑games to help you build vocabulary and common phrases in more than 45 languages, with bite‑sized lessons designed to be completed in about five minutes a day.
Drops is designed for both beginners and experts who want to grow their foreign language vocabulary.
The free version of the app offers five-minute lessons per day. You can get unlimited access and premium features for $11.99 per month or $79.99 per year. The app is available on both iOS and Android.
This story was originally published in March 2026 and is updated regularly with new information.

articles.title: 'You can't legislate for the idiots': The UK government is finally cracking down on e-bike operators and nuisance parking — here's how to have your say
articles.text:
'Wild west' e-bike parking is finally being targeted by the UK government — but will its plan really work?
"You can't legislate for the idiots", says the Transport Secretary
If you've ever used a shared e-bike in the UK, you'll know it can be a really convenient, cheap, and environmentally friendly way to get around. They're good exercise, too. But until now, their use has been largely unregulated — and that's created some big downsides, too.
Now Downing Street wants to change that. The UK government is putting forward a swathe of measures to tackle issues like e-bikes blocking the pavement, too few parking spaces, and problems with anti-social rider behaviour.
“I think the fact that we are consulting on this new licensing regime means that we can start to bring some order to the chaos that some people see in some parts of big cities where these e-bike schemes, rental schemes have popped up,” Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander told the Press Association.
"There are a small minority of people who choose to behave recklessly but sadly, that is true of any type of way that people move around in a town or a city, and you can’t legislate for the idiots. But we can take sensible steps to give local leaders more power over the way in which these types of schemes operate,” she added.
A law has already been passed to begin the process of licensing e-bike hire companies. What's new now is this public consultation, running until the end of 2026, during which citizens, lawmakers and e-bike companies can have their say.
Why is 'nuisance' e-bike parking still such a problem?
It's estimated that there are around 350,000 shared e-bike trips every day in London alone, and that's a lot of bicycles. In most regions, there are no rules about where bikes can be picked up from or left, and not enough designated parking spaces to go around — the accompanying apps simply direct users towards them via GPS.
That's led to plenty of overcrowding on the pavements, and e-bikes being left in areas that make life difficult or dangerous for pedestrians. Earlier this year, e-bike hire operator Lime apologised for one of its parked e-bikes forcing a blind man into the road with his guide dog. There have also been issues with riders not being able to complete journeys because of the patchwork of different rules and guidelines across individual London boroughs.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Anti-social behaviour from riders has been an issue, too: Users who hire the cycles when drunk, or in a way that endangers themselves other people around them. There have long been calls for the operators to take more responsibility for how their bikes are used.
Making the operators more responsible is difficult for councils that have no real powers and very little data about how the e-bikes are being used — at the moment they're relying on the goodwill of the e-bike companies and the voluntary agreements that are in place, which is something the government wants to improve upon and formalise.
What is the government proposing to do about it?
There's quite a bit to dig into when it comes to the new measures. The government says there will be new parking plans that make sure e-bikes aren't "inconveniencing the public" when they're not in use, and there will be fleet management plans too, designed to reduce bike overcrowding (think limits on the total number of bikes in an area).
In addition, fleets of bicycles will need to be properly maintained under the new guidelines, so you can be sure that you're getting on something safe when you ride a shared e-bike — and that pedestrians and other road users aren't going to be put in danger by a faulty battery or wheel.
Speaking of pedestrian safety, the proposals might also potentially cover insurance requirements for operators, so they'd be able to pay out compensation if someone got hit by a shared cycle and its rider. More parking spaces for e-bikes and more accountability for operators in regards to how their e-bikes are used are also planned.
With stronger rules in force, and closer partnerships with the e-bike companies involved, councils will have greater powers to punish those who are found to be in breach of the guidelines — whether that's leaving an e-bike in an appropriate and unsafe space, or getting behind the handlebars while intoxicated.
What have the e-bike companies said?
The e-bike companies are largely for the proposals. Certainty over the legitimacy of bicycle hire schemes means investment can be increased, while the confusion over current guidelines — which are largely voluntary and vary from council to council — isn't really helping any of the parties involved. Under the government's new proposals, hire companies might also get funding help for infrastructure like parking bays.
"We welcome the government’s consultation on national standards for shared e-bikes," said Georgia Heathman, Public Policy Manager at Bolt. "98% of Bolt rides already end with a correctly parked bike, which shows what clear rules and effective management can achieve. We want to see that standard applied consistently across the country, and support the consultation’s ambition to give local leaders the tools to licence schemes that suit their communities and raise the national bar."
"We recognise the current patchwork approach is confusing for riders, councils and operators, all of whom deserve greater clarity and certainty," commented Wayne Ting, CEO at Lime, which is the largest shared e-bike operator in the UK. "Today’s consultation is an important step forward."
The CEO of Forest, Agustin Guilisasti, chimed in with a call for "national standards", and for a "coherent, well-regulated" system going forward, while Prime Minister Andy Burnham said one of the main aims of the new consultation would be "giving communities more control over where [shared e-bikes] are parked and making sure companies and riders play by the rules".
Will this really solve the problem?
Time will tell, but there seems to be cautious optimism among those involved at the moment that new laws and regulations will make a genuine difference to the experience of shared e-bikes for those riding them and the general public at large. Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander is taking the lead here, promising that local leaders will ultimately get powers to "stop nuisance parking, tackle anti-social behaviour and make journeys safer".
"We hope licensing can be a way to provide suitable and well-enforced parking spaces for this highly popular, low carbon mode of travel and so help the government deliver on its own commitment to scale up shared mobility," Richard Dilks, CEO of shared transport organisation Collaborative Mobility UK (CoMoUK), told TechRadar. "Any regulation should protect the many benefits that these schemes bring, including boosting the rates of active travel, improving air quality, and reducing traffic congestion."
Mike Wordingham, Head of Policy at the Royal National Institute of Blind People, acknowledged that "tackling rider behaviour will be difficult, and it’s vital the desire for local flexibility doesn’t lead to a patchwork of regulations and inconsistency in implementing them".
"There's clearly a case for regulation of dockless e-bikes to ensure everyone can travel around cities safely and quickly," Anthony Breach, Director of Policy and Research at Centre for Cities, told TechRadar. "A key test will be how much responsibility the mayors have — different cities are different, and it's right that mayors can design policy on dockless bikes that work for the city as a whole."
"Regulations have costs, and we should expect there to be at least a small impact on cost and convenience," adds Breach. "But the lack of regulation of dockless bikes is also affecting the convenience and costs of other highway users, too. The challenge for government and the mayors is maximising convenience while minimising price across every form of urban transport."
E-bike operators are already testing in-app features like intoxication tests (via a response time analysis) and safe parking checks (via user-taken photos scanned by AI), but the consultation is an opportunity for everyone to have their say on the best rules and regulations going forward — you can contribute yourself here.
Follow TechRadar on Google News and add us as a preferred source to get our expert news, reviews, and opinion in your feeds.
Dave is a freelance tech journalist who has been writing about gadgets, apps and the web for more than two decades. Based out of Stockport, England, on TechRadar you'll find him covering news, features and reviews, particularly for phones, tablets and wearables. Working to ensure our breaking news coverage is the best in the business over weekends, David also has bylines at Gizmodo, T3, PopSci and a few other places besides, as well as being many years editing the likes of PC Explorer and The Hardware Handbook.

articles.title: Top 10 Canal+ : les séries incontournables à ne surtout pas rater en novembre
articles.text:
Canal+ : notre top 10 des meilleures séries à voir en streaming en novembre 2026
Pas besoin de scroller pendant des heures sur l'application Canal+ avant de trouver une bonne série à regarder. Les Numériques vous guide avec sa sélection des 10 meilleures séries à voir en novembre 2026.
Que voir sur Canal+ et son application en novembre 2026 si on aime les séries ? L'offre de la chaîne cryptée est large entre ses propositions exclusives et ses créations originales.
Le catalogue contient aussi de nombreuses séries provenant d'autres plateformes de SVOD comme Apple TV et Paramount+, accessibles aux abonnés via différentes offres Canal+.
Choisir son programme peut donc vite devenir compliqué alors pour vous éviter de chercher pendant de longues minutes, Les Numériques a sélectionné pour vous, comme le mois dernier, son top des 10 séries à ne pas manquer sur Canal+ ce mois-ci.
Pour rappel, les séries Apple TV, Paramount+ et Ciné+ OCS sont accessibles via les offres Canal+ Ciné Séries et Canal+ La Totale.
Quelles sont les meilleures séries à voir sur Canal+ en novembre 2026 ?
Singapura
Justine débarque à Singapour, bien décidée à se réinventer et à offrir un nouveau départ à son couple. Elle découvre la petite communauté très policée des expatriés français et se laisse aussitôt fasciner par Élisa, un esprit libre, fantasque et tourmenté qui détonne dans ce cercle fermé. Lorsque celle-ci est assassinée, Justine se retrouve embarquée aux côtés de l’inspecteur Adam Wong dans une enquête où le vernis de l’expatriation se craquelle peu à peu.
La nouvelle création originale de Canal+ nous emporte dans l'univers des "expats" de la cité-état asiatique. Un monde à part, entre gratte-ciel et mangrove, propice à un thriller moite et suffoquant, où crimes et adultères vont de paire. Une série d'enquête certes un peu trop dans les rails du genre, mais avec un beau récit d'émancipation féminine et un casting solide, dont Naïlia Harzoune (66-5), Soji Arai (Tokyo Vice) et India Hair (Polar Park). Du Canal+ classique certes, mais efficace.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Tulsa King
Dwight "The General" Manfredi est un ancien parrain de la Mafia italienne à New York. Alors qu'il sort de 25 ans de prison pour couvrir son boss, ce dernier l'envoie, le contraint d'aller s'installer à Tulsa, dans l'Oklahoma. Face à cet exil forcé dans un lieu plus qu'improbable, Dwight Manfredi décide de monter son équipe formée de personnes très singulières. Il espère ainsi établir un nouvel empire.
Sylvester Stallone est grandiose dans cette série créée par Taylor Sheridan, le scénariste prolifique derrière Yellowstone. L’acteur de 80 ans donne tout ce qu’il a dans le rôle de ce mafieux prêt à tout pour se construire une nouvelle vie après un quart de siècle derrière barreaux. Il est entouré de second rôles qui lui tiennent tête sans sourciller pour une série pleine de drame, d’action, et de retournements de situation.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Yellowjackets
À la suite d'un accident d'avion, les jeunes membres d'une équipe de football féminin sont contraintes de survivre dans un environnement sauvage et inhospitalier. 30 ans plus tard, on retrouve ce qu'il reste de ses survivantes et découvre comment elles s'en sont sorties.
Yellowjackets rappellera de bons souvenirs aux fans de slashers et d'adolescents massacrés. Mais la série ne s'arrête pas là, et offre une structure narrative avec deux temporalités, l'une en 1996, l'autre en 2021, qui dialoguent et font avancer une histoire mystérieuse de crash d'avion et de cannibalisme. Belle réussite d'horreur, de tension à couper au couteau et de personnages finement écrits, elle vaut aussi le détour pour son casting féminin de qualité : Mélanie Lynskey, Christina Ricci, Juliette Lewis, Ella Purnell, Sophie Thatcher...
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Devil in Disguise
Entre 1972 et 1978, trente-trois jeunes hommes ont été kidnappés, assassinés puis enterrés sous la maison de leur meurtrier John Wayne Gacy. Et pendant toutes ces années, personne ne s'est douté de rien. Sympathique et drôle, cette figure respectée dans sa communauté était même bénévole auprès des enfants malades qu'il divertissait déguisé en clown. À travers les multiples facettes de John Wayne Gacy et les récits bouleversants des victimes et de leurs proches, ce sont les défaillances institutionnelles qui sont pointées, tout comme les occasions manquées et les préjugés de la société qui ont permis à ce meurtrier de continuer à tuer.
Aux antipodes de l'anthologie Monstre de Netflix, cette série examine l'histoire de John Wayne Gacy avec beaucoup de tact et de respect envers ses victimes. Au lieu de verser dans le sensationnalisme, le show se concentre sur le coût humain des crimes de Gacy et trouve en Michael Chernus un interprète aussi glaçant que perturbant. On tient là une série éprouvante, émouvante, mais surtout un récit true crime des plus réfléchis sur le sujet de ce tueur en série notoire.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Apollo has fallen
Zara Taylor du MI6, les services secrets britanniques, et Vincent Taleb, ancien agent de protection rapprochée du ministre français de la Défense, coopèrent de nouveau quand un avion est détourné au large des côtes libyennes. Cette première attaque marque le début d’une vaste conspiration menée par un violent mercenaire russe, Yuri Mishkin. Alors qu’un virus mortel menace de décimer l’Europe, les deux agents doivent agir vite pour stopper Yuri et ses complices, dont un traître dans leurs propres rangs.
Plus ambitieuse, plus rythmée et surtout plus généreuse en action, Apollo Has Fallen corrige en partie les défauts de Paris Has Fallen et franchit un véritable cap. Sans parvenir à se hisser au niveau des meilleures productions du genre, la série Canal+ s'impose néanmoins comme un divertissement solide, efficace et suffisamment spectaculaire pour tenir le spectateur en haleine jusqu'au bout. Une deuxième saison qui montre que la franchise a clairement les moyens de ses ambitions, même si on en attendra plus d'audace dans la mise en scène.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Dark Matter
Jason Dessen, professeur de physique à Chicago, est enlevé un soir alors qu’il rentre chez lui. Lorsqu’il reprend connaissance, son épouse n’est plus la sienne, son fils n’existe pas et il découvre qu’il est devenu un scientifique célèbre à l’origine d’une invention révolutionnaire. Jason comprend bientôt qu’il a été projeté dans une réalité issue d’un choix qu’il aurait pu faire autrefois. Pour retrouver sa véritable famille, il doit traverser différentes versions de son existence et affronter un adversaire qui le connaît mieux que personne.
Adapté du roman de science-fiction de Blake Crouch, ce thriller atmosphérique et époustouflant plonge le spectateur dans une histoire de multivers passionnante. Joel Edgerton, Jennifer Connelly et le reste de la distribution sont impeccables, la mise en scène et les décors sont soignés et l'histoire sur fond de crise existentielle captivera les adeptes de séries aux concepts pointus dès son premier épisode.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
MobLand
MobLand
Harry Da Souza, un homme de main débrouillard, se voit plongé en plein conflit entre deux familles criminelles, qui cherchent à prendre le pouvoir au risque de renverser des empires et de ruiner des vies.
Si l'intrigue de cette nouvelle série sur fond de gangsters londoniens sent un peu le réchauffé et ne révolutionne pas son genre, MobLand se regarde sans déplaisir. Le show vaut surtout le détour pour l'élégance de sa production, son casting soigné et un Tom Hardy fabuleux et charismatique. Bref, une série très solide qui est revenue récemment avec sa deuxième saison.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Slow Horses
Une équipe d’agents secrets britanniques est mise au placard par le MI5 suite aux erreurs qu’ils ont commises en mission. Placés sous les ordres d’un chef aussi brillant qu’irascible, le célèbre Jackson Lamb, ils naviguent dans le monde de l’espionnage, où règnent les faux-semblants, pour défendre la Grande-Bretagne contre les forces ennemies.
Slow Horses met en scène des espions britanniques qui regardent leur carrière mourir. Portée par un Gary Oldman caustique dans le rôle de Jackson Lamb, la série propose une intrigue captivante sur fond d'humour noir pinçant et introduit une galerie de personnages soit résolus à accepter leur sort, soit avides de remonter les échelons du MI5 et de redorer leur blason.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Opérations Spéciales : Lioness
Inspirée d'un programme militaire américain, cette série suit le quotidien de Joe, officier de pointe de la CIA dans la guerre contre le terrorisme, dans sa quête d'équilibre entre sa vie personnelle et professionnelle. Le programme Lioness supervisé fait appel à la jeune Marine Cruz Manuelos, un peu brutale mais passionnée, pour opérer sous couverture aux côtés de Joe et contrecarrer le projet d'un nouveau 11 septembre.
Zoe Saldaña, Nicole Kidman, Dave Annable ou encore Michael Kelly sont au casting de ce thriller explosif signé Taylor Sheridan (Yellowstone). Lioness est une série qui mélange espionnage, opérations militaires et contre-terrorisme dans une intrigue finement ficelée qui tient le spectateur en haleine d'épisode en épisode, avec en son cœur des personnages diablement bien incarnés et surtout très intéressants à découvrir.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :
Prisoner
Lorsqu'un convoi pénitentiaire est pris d’assaut, Amber Todd, agente chargée du transfert, se retrouve prise au piège avec Tibor Stone - ancien tueur d’élite devenu témoin clé contre Pegasus, le réseau criminel qu’il a autrefois servi. Pourchassés par ce puissant conglomérat du crime et par des autorités corrompues, Amber et Tibor, deux inconnus que tout oppose, sont forcés de fuir ensemble…
Tahar Rahim et Izuka Hoyle forment un duo de choc dans ce thriller d'action bourré d'une tension que seuls les Britanniques semblent parfaitement bien maîtriser. Avec six épisodes au compteur, Prisoner captive l'attention dès ses premières minutes et ne lâche pas son spectateur avant son dénouement, faisant avancer son intrigue à un rythme soutenu et reposant sur une distribution impeccable pour maintenir les yeux du spectateur rivés sur l'écran.
- Regardez la bande-annonce de la série :

articles.title: Pas de Smart TV ? Pour le 11.11, la Xiaomi TV Box S 3 passe à 81,03€ seulement
articles.text:
Le 11.11 d’AliExpress ouvre la saison des promotions avant le Black Friday, et les boîtiers qui modernisent un vieux téléviseur en profitent. La Xiaomi TV Box S 3e génération passe à 81,03 € avec le code CLU13, pour un lecteur 4K Dolby Vision sous Google TV qui fait l’impasse sur l’Ethernet.
Troisième version du boîtier de salon de Xiaomi, la TV Box S 3e génération apporte Google TV à n’importe quel écran doté d’une prise HDMI. Elle repose sur une puce Amlogic S905X5M gravée en 6 nm et lit la 4K à 60 images par seconde, avec Dolby Vision, HDR10+ et Dolby Atmos. Pour le 11.11, elle est affichée à 81,03 € au lieu de 99,43 € sur AliExpress avec le code CLU13, soit 18,40 € de moins.
L’offre vise d’abord ceux qui veulent rendre connecté un téléviseur ou un vidéoprojecteur sans changer d’écran.
La Xiaomi TV Box S 3e génération descend à 81,03 € au lieu de 99,43 € sur AliExpress, à condition de saisir le code CLU13 au moment de payer.
Pourquoi choisir la Xiaomi TV Box S 3e génération ?
- L’image HDR complète : Le boîtier lit le Dolby Vision, le HDR10+, le HDR10 et le HLG, ce qui évite de perdre le HDR d’un film selon le format retenu par la plateforme. Reste à vérifier ce que votre téléviseur accepte.
- Un son prêt pour le home cinéma : La prise en charge du Dolby Atmos et du DTS:X permet d’envoyer à une barre de son ou à un ampli compatible la piste audio d’origine des films qui en disposent.
- Une génération plus musclée : Xiaomi annonce 25 % de puissance processeur et 130 % de puissance graphique en plus par rapport au modèle précédent. Le Wi-Fi 6 bi-bande aide à garder un flux 4K stable sans câble.
Du salon au vidéoprojecteur, là où ce boîtier a sa place
Son premier terrain est le téléviseur 4K dont l’interface a vieilli, ou qui n’a jamais été connecté. Google TV regroupe alors les applications de streaming dans un seul menu, et la certification Widevine L1 autorise la lecture en haute définition sur les services qui l’exigent. Le boîtier sert aussi de relais depuis un smartphone, pour diffuser une vidéo sur grand écran. Avec 97 x 97 x 17 mm et 91 grammes, il se glisse derrière un meuble TV ou à côté d’un vidéoprojecteur.
Il convient bien à une chambre, à une pièce secondaire ou à un vidéoprojecteur dépourvu de système connecté. Nous ne l’avons pas testé, mais ses caractéristiques dessinent aussi ses limites. Avec 2 Go de mémoire vive, les applications les plus gourmandes peuvent le pousser dans ses retranchements, et ses 32 Go de stockage, non extensibles par carte SD, ne conviennent pas à une grosse bibliothèque de films en local. Ceux qui misent sur Plex, Kodi ou un réseau filaire trouveront mieux ailleurs.
Face au Google TV Streamer et aux Fire TV Stick, un compromis à connaître
Le Google TV Streamer va plus loin, avec 4 Go de mémoire vive et un port Ethernet Gigabit, tandis que l’Apple TV 4K s’adresse d’abord aux utilisateurs de l’écosystème Apple. Face aux clés HDMI d’entrée de gamme, la Xiaomi se distingue par sa puissance de traitement et ses formats HDR et audio. Elle ne figure pas parmi les modèles recommandés dans notre guide des meilleures box TV, faute de test de notre part, et l’Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Plus y reste notre choix pour la majorité des utilisateurs.
✅ Les points forts
- Dolby Vision, HDR10+, Dolby Atmos et DTS:X pris en charge
- Interface Google TV et certification Widevine L1
- Wi-Fi 6 bi-bande et sortie HDMI 2.1
- Format compact de 91 grammes
- Puce 6 nm plus puissante que la génération précédente
❌ Les limites
- 2 Go de mémoire vive, sans marge pour les usages lourds
- Pas de port Ethernet et un seul port USB 2.0
- 32 Go de stockage, non extensible par carte SD
- Un prix bien supérieur à celui de nos précédents bons plans sur ce boîtier
Le code CLU13 se saisit à l’étape du paiement sur AliExpress : vérifiez que le total affiché tombe bien à 81,03 € avant de valider la commande.
À 81,03 €, la Xiaomi TV Box S 3e génération reste un moyen simple d’apporter Google TV, le Dolby Vision et le Dolby Atmos à un écran qui en est privé. Elle s’adresse à ceux qui regardent surtout des plateformes de streaming et veulent un boîtier discret, branché en Wi-Fi. Ses formats d’image et de son la placent au-dessus des clés HDMI les plus simples.
Le prix demande en revanche du recul : nous avons relayé ce même boîtier à 69,51 € au début du 11.11, et à moins de 50 € à plusieurs reprises cette année. Si vous pouvez attendre le Black Friday du 27 novembre, surveillez son prix. Ceux qui ont besoin d’une connexion filaire, d’un gros stockage ou d’un lecteur pour Plex et Kodi passeront leur chemin. Pour du streaming au quotidien, l’essentiel est là.

articles.title: Ranking de YouTube en España: la lista de los 10 videos musicales más populares hoy
articles.text:
En un mundo moderno tan vertiginoso y estresante es normal que la gente busque diversas maneras para relajarse y olvidarse un poco de los problemas del día, ya sea una salida con amigos, ver películas en familia, ver alguna serie antes de dormir, hacer yoga o bien recurrir a los videos de YouTube.
YouTube, surgida en el año 2005, se ha convertido en la biblioteca digital de videos más grande del mundo y ahí se puede encontrar desde música, pasando por historias de terror hasta llegar a los famosos clips ASMR entre millones de canales.
A la plataforma, que además es el segundo sitio más popular del mundo sólo detrás de Google, se suben más de 500 horas de contenido cada minuto y se estima que las ganancias para la red de videos llega a los 15 mil millones de dólares al trimestre.
A las estadísticas se añade que YouTube tiene presencia en al menos 104 países, disponible en un total de 80 idiomas.
Según la plataforma, alrededor del mundo los usuarios ven 5 mil millones de videos al día, por lo que al ser una tarea titánica el decidir qué ver y no perderse entre tantas novedades, la plataforma lanzó en el 2018 diversos charts en donde se puede consultar cuáles son los videos más vistos de la semana (general), los videos musicales más reproducidos en los últimos días y las tendencias del día, que se actualiza en tiempo real.
Acá el listado de los videos que están en tendencia este sábado 7 de noviembre
1. Milko Freestyle (Video Oficial)Artista/canal: C. Tangana y Agorazein
2. DONDE ESTAN? cap. 11 - YOLAMASCARA FT 50 CENTArtista/canal: YOLAMASCARA
3. POKITOArtista/canal: Daddy Yankee
4. Lejos de Mi (Official Music Video)Artista/canal: Josue Rarujo
5. LAJA x ANUEL AA - TUSSI (Video Oficial)Artista/canal: LAJA
6. 2.0 2Artista/canal: l0rna
7. SHARINGANArtista/canal: La Pantera
8. La Pantera - COLOREAME (Visualizer) | FILIPENSESArtista/canal: La Pantera
9. La Pantera, Alea - TONY STARK (Visualizer) | FILIPENSESArtista/canal: La Pantera
10. Cartier RemixArtista/canal: El Americano 4KT y Lil Naay
Los inicios de YouTube
YouTube vio la luz en febrero de 2005, cuando tres antiguos empleados de la compañía de Paypal ―Chad Hurley, Steve Chen y Jawed Karim― se unieron y la crearon luego de que experimentaran dificultades para compartir entre sí un par de videos tras asistir a una fiesta.
El dominio fue activado el 14 de febrero de 2005 y casi un mes después, el 23 de abril, fue cargado el primer clip a la plataforma que llevaba por nombre “Me at the Zoo”. Fue cuestión de tiempo para que todo el mundo comenzara a cargar contenido y a compartir los enlaces a través de otras redes sociales como MySpace.
Una de las grandes empresas que vio el potencial de YouTube fue la marca Nike, que subió una publicidad protagonizada por Ronaldinho, lo que hizo que otras grandes compañías voltearan a ver a YouTube y se sintieran atraídas.
Tal fue la gran acogida de los internautas por YouTube que para diciembre de 2005 la plataforma pasó de las 50 millones de visitas al día a 250 millones de visualizaciones luego de que un canal subiera el clip musical Lazy Sunday, transmitido originalmente por Saturday Night Live.
Para el año siguiente, en el 2006, el sitio fue comparado por el gigante del internet, Google, por un valor de 1650 millones de dólares. En ese entonces eran visualizados 100 millones de videos al día y 65 mil clips se añadían a diario. También firmaron acuerdos con disqueras para poder reproducir videos musicales.
YouTube en la cultura popular
Desde que fue puesto en marcha, YouTube fue un sitio que llegó a hacer una revolución no sólo en internet, sino también en la forma en la que los usuarios miran contenido. Muestra de ello el reconocimiento que la revista Time le otorgó en noviembre del 2006 al ser nombrado el “Invento del Año”.
Convertido en el mejor medio de difusión, el gozar de tanta popularidad también ha metido a sus dueños en aprietos como cuando albergar peleas escolares o en donde hay bullying, clips relacionados al terrorismo, narcotráfico u otros temas considerados delicados por su contenido íntimo o por mostrar delitos como asesinatos y más.
Para Estados Unidos uno de los temas más delicados es el de los tiroteos escolares, por lo que YouTube ha estado más de una vez en el ojo del huracán por alojar contenido filmado por los atacantes, como fue el caso de la masacre de Virginia Tech, cuando Cho Seung-Hui, el atacante, subió previamente a los hechos un discurso.
Más recientemente, tras el surgimiento de la pandemia del coronavirus, también ha surgido inquietud sobre cómo la plataforma permite la monetización de contenido que puede ser engañoso y riesgoso para la población.
Aunque no todo es malo, pues a través de dicha plataforma muchas personas han podido ser reconocidas por su talento, como fue el caso de Susan Boyle, quien participó en el programa Britain’s Got Talent cuyo extracto subido a YouTube logró que la mujer pasara a ser una completa desconocida a una de las personas más viralizadas, famosas y aclamadas del internet.

articles.title: 'Cuts through dirt like a dorsal fin through water’ — I love how Shark’s transforming vacuum cleaner switches smoothly between upright and stick vac, while its smart suction devours dust in every situation
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The flexible 3-in-1 transforming design that allows you to easily switch between upright, stick and handheld vacuum might be the Shark PowerDetect Transformer’s most attention-grabbing feature. But what really impressed me is its strong suction and super-smart auto-detection — it adapts to different flooring, edges and quantities of dirt automatically, making sucking up dust, debris and even pet hair a breeze. Couple in how easy it is to empty and it’s an impressive vacuum that should make handling your whole home easy.
Reasons to buy
- + Transforming 3-in-1 design
- + Packed with smart auto-detection features
- + Superb suction
- + Easy to empty
Reasons to avoid
- - Upright mode quite unwieldy
- - Very loud
- - Wired only
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Shark PowerDetect Transformer: two-minute review
The Shark PowerDetect Transformer is a wired vacuum cleaner that combines an upright, stick and handheld vacuum all in one. It offers plenty of the premium features you might expect, including tangle-free brush bar and dirt-illuminating LED, but also comes crammed with smart features like automatic dirt, surface and edge detection.
The Shark PowerDetect Transformer admittedly isn’t the most easily wielded vacuum cleaner in its upright form — weighing in at 17.6 lbs / 8kg — but it has a trick up its sleeve. Press a single button and its vacuum pod pops off, turning it into a svelte stick vacuum with its own discrete dust bin. Need even more flexibility? Pop off the top section and it becomes a handy handheld vac. Switching between each system is seriously swift, which is really smart design.
On top of this, the PowerDetect Transformer also offers an excellent range of accessories for different tasks, so you’re not just limited to its talented DuoClean Detect nozzle. The HairPro Self-Cleaning Pet Power brush is great for getting pet hair off your rugs and furniture — with its anti-tangle tech preventing the bar getting clogged — and it also includes old classics like a crevice tool and a multi-surface brush. On top of this, it has built-in HEPA certified filtration and an anti-allergen seal, which the asthma sufferers in my house definitely appreciate.
In my book though, the thing that helps the PowerDetect Transformer rival the best vacuum cleaners is how hassle-free it makes sucking up crud from your carpets and hard flooring. Absolutely chock full of auto-detection features, it will dial the level of its suction up and down depending on your floor type, the amount of dirt it detects or the direction you’re dragging it in. Even smarter is its edge detection, which senses when you’re vacuuming against furniture and along room boundaries and directs its suction toward them to more completely do away with detritus.
I’ll admit that being smart doesn’t necessarily always translate being capable. Fortunately, all these smarts do make Shark’s vacuum seriously good at shifting dirt. Pretty much every test I put the PowerDetect Transformer through it aced, getting up coarse dirt from a hard floor and dust out of a shallow pile carpet in a single sweep. And when vacuuming room edges — the achilles heel of many vacuum cleaners — every single lentil I’d tossed down vanished in one movement. The fact pretty much all of this happened without me having to tap a single button is just the icing on the cake.
On top of this, its brush bars were able to remove a disturbing quantity of cat hair from my upholstery without getting clogged, making it easy to clean up after my champion shedder. However, while the bars themselves were great at avoiding tangles, I did find that a couple of times a snarl of hair got caught around the exit into the cyclone chamber, causing it to get slightly backed up. This only happened a few times and won’t matter much as long as you empty the vacuum often enough to stop the hose getting backed up, but it’s worth bearing in mind for the hairiest households.
Once you’re finished, emptying the Shark is also seriously straightforward. After using either its handheld or stick modes, clipping its vacuum pod back on triggers its self-emptying cycle, rapidly emptying its smaller dust bin. And when you want to empty the vacuum pod itself, all you have to do is press the bin switch to detach the larger bin, hold it over your bin and unhook a catch to open the bottom and jettison its contents.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Perhaps the one criticism I do have of the PowerDetect Transformer’s performance is it’s very loud — measuring it with a sound level meter, it hit 74dB during upright use and a raucous 82dB during its self-cleaning cycle. So if you have sensitive neighbors or, like mine, your cat tends toward the scaredy, it might not be the one for you.
Still though, all in all, the Shark PowerDetect Transformer is an impressive vacuum cleaner. Not only is it powerful, it’s smart, easy to use and flexible enough to vacuum pretty much every area of your home. Yes, wireless is always a nice to have — although its 8m cable meant I didn’t miss this as much as I thought I would — it’s loud and it occasionally gets a bit backed up. But I’m happy to forgive these minor quibbles given how much easier it makes day-to-day cleaning.
Shark PowerDetect Transformer review: price & availability
- Launched June 30, 2026
- Costs $529.99 / £499.99 / AU$699.99
Having launched on June 30, 2026, the Shark PowerDetect Transformer is widely available now. It goes for a list price of $529.99 / £499.99 / AU$699.99 — although at the time of writing, in the US, you can use the code TRIO at the checkout to save $130, bringing it down to $399.99.
That price is hardly chicken feed but, for what you’re getting, it’s still reasonable value. For example, the Shark PowerDetect Cordless — our current pick for the best vacuum cleaner out there — is priced at a roughly equivalent $429.99 / £499.99 / AU$849.99 and while unlike the Transformer it’s fully wireless, it can’t convert into a full, high-capacity upright. Meanwhile, the premium Dyson Gen5detect is much more spendy at $949.99 / £769.99 / AU$1,549, while rocking relatively similar features.
In return for your spend, you’re not only getting three vacuums in one but also a solid range of accessories. It comes with the classics such as brush and crevice tools but it also packs a stair tool, the HairPro Pet Power Brush for powered action against pet fuzz and an anti-allergen dusting brush. It also comes with a handy accessory bag to keep them all in.
Finally, the Shark PowerDetect Transformer comes in two tasty colorways: Chimera Blue — a dusky sky blue — and Deep Sage Green. Both of these really pop, especially with those gold highlights, although I’d say I just marginally prefer the former.

Shark PowerDetect Transformer review: design
- Flexible, modular design
- Stuffed with auto-detection features
- Wired only
Okay, I’ll admit when I first heard the name Shark Transformer, I was hoping I was going to be getting a toy robot that converted into a toothy, predatory fish. Fortunately, the design of this vacuum cleaner is nearly as cool. Its modular design makes it easy to switch between three different modes — heavy-duty upright vacuum cleaner, lightweight stick vac and flexible handheld — at the click of a button.
Moreover, unlike previous 3-in-1 vacuum cleaners Shark has created, this one is a hoseless design, meaning you don’t have to hook and unhook elephant trunk tubing every time you want to switch modes. Sliding the vacuum pod on and off the wand, it just clicks into place and connects to the vacuum’s airlock in one smooth movement. It’s clever design and makes selecting the right tool for your job feel effortless.
Naturally, as a result of this protean form, it’s quite hard to comment on the overall size and weight of the device. Because in its upright vacuum final evolution it’s a pretty bulky and hefty beast but pop off a couple of sections and suddenly you’re left with something super light and flexible. So it’s a bit of a quantum vacuum cleaner: a superposition of heavy and light at the same time.
Fortunately, when it comes to its appearance, the PowerDetect Transformer is far less paradoxical. I’m definitely picking up what Shark is throwing down here: in its stick and handheld modes, the Transformer looks seriously sleek and although the vacuum pod is pretty hulking, it’s still excellently engineered. On top of this, the colorways on offer are stunning — the deep sage green colorway I tested looks great but the chimera blue version is genuinely droolworthy. Genuinely, it gives me the same vibes as my sky blue MacBook Air and I wants it.
Setting the Shark up for the first time is pretty straightforward, even if compared to other wired vacuums there is some assembly required. Essentially, all you need to do is click the wand into place on the nozzle, slide the vacuum pod into its home on the stick and insert the hand vacuum into the top.
After this, you’re basically all set to start sucking up grit right away, because the Transformer neither has smart home features to set up or battery to charge. And don’t sweat this last omission too much — its eight-meter cable means you should be able to comfortably reach most areas of your home.
Alongside all of these modules, the Transformer also features all of the usual suspects in terms of accessories, such as the brush and the crevice tool. However, it doesn’t stop there: it also includes Shark’s HairPro Self-Cleaning Pet Power brush, a miniature brush bar tool with anti-wrap technology for getting pet hair and dander out from carpets and upholstery.
But by far its smartest tool is its DuoClean Detect nozzle. On top of its self-cleaning brush roll that picks up hair without getting tangled and targeted LED lighting for showing up barely visible specs of dirt, it’s also absolutely crammed with smart auto-detection features. Whether it’s sensing your floor type, adjusting to the quantity of dirt, directing suction forward or backward depending on the direction you’re moving in or automatically targeting its air inflow to gulp down detritus right up to the edge of rooms, it does all the hard work so you can just focus on practicing your Freddie Mercury impression.
Given all of these auto-detection features, the controls on the Shark PowerDetect Transformer are almost comically uncomplicated. There’s an on button… and that’s basically all you need to understand. If you’re a real control freak, you can manually set its suction to match hard floor, shallow pile or deep pile carpet but honestly I never needed to manually control this, as its auto-detect features did a perfectly effective job at dialing its suction up and down.
Finally, given I live with someone who both suffers from asthma and has the nasal sensitivity of a sommelier with a Neti pot, I definitely appreciate how the Transformer handles dust and disagreeable odors. Its HEPA-certified filtration and anti-allergen seal keeps all of that bronchial-irritating crud locked away. And once you’ve popped one of Shark’s odor-neutralizing cartridges into the nozzle, you can dial its stench-scrubbing capabilities up or down to remove any distressing scents the grime kicks up.
- Design score: 4.5 / 5
Shark PowerDetect Transformer review: performance
- Fantastic suction in almost every scenario
- Emptying is wonderfully easy
- Startlingly loud
Given how clever its features are, this vacuum cleaner is clearly a real bright shark. But how does that translate into real-world performance? After all, what good is the cold, calculating mind of a great white if it’s stuck in the ungainly body of a sunfish? Fortunately, you don’t need to worry on this front — the Shark PowerDetect Transformer cuts through dirt like a dorsal fin through water.
As I’ve already remarked above, the bulk and weight of the Transformer really depends on which mode you use it in. In its upright form, it’s definitely on the husky side — I lift weights multiple times a week, yet I still felt the effort of dragging it round. Fortunately, its two-axis joint makes it pretty easy to maneuver around furniture and once you strip it back to its stick or handheld forms, it’s considerably easier to wield.
Keen to really put the PowerDetect Transformer through its paces, I not only vacuumed my house top to bottom but conducted our full battery of standardized tests. First off, I sprinkled the contents of a teabag on a range of different flooring types to simulate the finer dust the Transformer would have to tackle. On my laminate flooring, the Transformer scarfed down those loose leaves in a single pass — even when repeating this test on my medium-pile carpet, the vacuum cleaner didn’t leave a single scrap behind.
Wanting to see how it fared with more substantial debris, I tried this same test with a small quantity of lentils. Once again, on a hard floor, the Shark snorted up every single pulse without hesitation. Admittedly, when I tried this out on carpet, it left behind three lentils out of about 50. But with a single swipe backward, its automatic direction sensing flipped the direction of its suction and it wolfed them down without issue.
Even trickier debris like pet hair didn’t seem to faze it. Trying it out on a ball of fuzz from my cat’s brush, the vacuum wolfed it down like cotton candy. I even put it to work on the cat’s favorite chair — which was so disgustingly furry that our previous vacuum cleaner had threatened to take industrial action — and yet Shark’s anti-hair wrap tool cut through it easily. And despite going up against upholstery more covered in hair than Hugh Jackman, it lived up to its name and didn’t get clogged or tangled.
So, all in all, I found its suction pretty impressive. But even more noteworthy are how those smarts I mentioned above improve cleaning performance across the board. Thanks to the Transformer’s Dirt Detect feature, during normal cleaning it regularly dialled up its suction strength to tackle denser piles of dust without me having to even think about it. And its edge-of-room performance is fantastic — trying to vacuum up lentils I scattered right up to the baseboard, the vacuum’s Edge Detect feature targeted its suction to pick up every last legume in a single sweep.
The Transformer’s other modes don’t offer quite as much smarts or power as the upright mode but they’re just as capable when tackling their own respective niches. The stick vacuum offers the same level of flexibility but a much lighter weight, making it the perfect tool for a quick runaround in a single room. Meanwhile, its handheld mode made short work of cleaning problem areas like the inside of my sofa and raised surfaces like my piano — without a bulky cyclone chamber attached, it felt so much more flexible than any other convertible vacuum handheld I’ve used.
And once you’re done cleaning, emptying the Transformer feels like a breeze, especially compared to older vacuums. Once you’ve used the stick or handheld vacuums, all you need to do is re-attach the vacuum pod and it will automatically suck out all the dust you’ve gathered into that main chamber.
Clearing out the vacuum pod itself is almost as easy. Detach it using the eject button and the dust bin and cyclone section come away, leaving the filter and vacuum components behind. Then all you need to do is open the bottom clip above the bin and it empties downward — far easier than banging it upside down against the bin till something finally dislodges.
Easy to clean though the Transformer is, I still wouldn’t say this process is absolutely foolproof. One thing I noticed a couple of times when emptying it out is that occasionally hair clogs would get snagged in the airlock into the vacuum pod, meaning that long fibers would start clogging up the main cyclone. Now, both my feline and my human housemates are world champion shedders, meaning this issue might not affect you as often, but it does make me worry you could quickly lose suction if you don’t stay on top of this.
One other slight drawback to the Transformer is a direct consequence of all its convenience and power: the noise. Reaching a volume of 74dB in upright mode and max volume of 82dB during its self-cleaning cycle, it hits the same rough volume as heavy traffic or a blender. While this didn’t bother the humans in my house that much, my cat HATED it — he found the noise while vacuuming upsetting enough but the automatic cleaning cycle sent him flying out of the room like he’d witnessed the Terminator itself. Turns out machines bellowing in rage without apparent human input is where he nopes out.
Ongoing maintenance of the device is a lot less stressful, fortunately. Although you need to clean the pre-motor filters of both chambers every month, the hand vac’s post-motor filter only needs cleaning every six months and replacing every 2.5 years, while the upright’s post-motor filter only needs cleaning once a year and replacing every three. Occasionally, you might also need to wipe those smart sensors to ensure they continue functioning properly but, all in all, this isn’t particularly punishing.
- Performance score: 4.5 / 5
Should I buy the Shark PowerDetect Transformer?
| Attribute | Notes | Score | 
|---|---|---|
| Value | Undeniably sits at the pricier end of the market. But given its 3-in-1 functionality, smart features and accessories, you’re getting a whole lot of vacuum cleaner in return for that spend. | 4/5 | 
| Design | Flexible, 3-in-1 modular design makes it easy to use in a whole load of scenarios, HEPA-certified filtration and odor-neutralising technology, no battery but 8m cable goes a long way toward making up for this. | 4.5/5 | 
| Performance | Wolfs down dust and debris on hard floors and carpet alike, expertly handles hair, auto-detection features optimize suction for every scenario, super easy to empty, loud enough to strike fear into the heart of the most unflinching feline. | 4.5/5 | 
Buy it if…
You don’t want to buy separate handheld, stick and upright vacuums
While stick vacuums are super versatile and handhelds are essential for vacuuming upholstery and raised surfaces, neither has the capacity and suction of a full upright. The PowerDetect Transformer gives you the benefit of all three in one package.
You want smart suction for every surface
The Shark’s auto-detect features mean it automatically tailors its suction power depending on the surface you’re vacuuming, how much dirt it detects, the direction it’s moving and even when you’re vacuuming room edges.
Don’t buy it if…
You hate trailing cables
Given it lacks a battery, you’ll always have to use the PowerDetect Transformer hooked up to a socket. Its 8m cable will still give you a lot of range though.
You (or your pet) has sensitive ears
Maxing out at 82dB during its cleaning cycle, this vacuum cleaner is not for the faint of heart. If you’re worried about upsetting your neighbours with your midnight vacuuming, this one might not be for you.
Shark PowerDetect Transformer review: also consider

| Runtime in Boost mode | N/A | 15 mins | 14 mins |

Shark PowerDetect Cordless Stick Vacuum
If you want all of the Transformer’s fancy PowerDetect features but aren’t bothered about its larger capacity, the 0.7L Shark PowerDetect Cordless Stick Vacuum is a great alternative. Yes, it comes in at roughly the same price — $429.99 / £499.99 / AU$849.99 — but as its moniker implies, it also eschews wires, making it the perfect choice for anyone who wants a super-smart, lightweight vacuum that can tackle dirt pretty much anywhere. Read our full Shark PowerDetect Cordless Stick Vacuum review.
Dyson Gen5detect
There’s a reason that the Dyson Gen5detect is our premium pick for best vacuum cleaner. Yes, part of that reason is its $949.99 / £769.99 / AU$1,549 price tag. But it’s also because of its superb suction, fantastic smart features and great battery life. Aside from capacity, the only area that the Shark PowerDetect Transformer has it beat is in vacuuming the edges of rooms, but otherwise if you’re looking for the best deluxe dirt-sucker out there the Dyson Gen5detect is likely it. Read our full Dyson Gen5detect review.
How I tested the Shark PowerDetect Transformer
- Tested it for several weeks
- Tried it out on a range of flooring and with different materials
- Set it to work on shed pet hair
I tested the Shark PowerDetect Transformer over a period of several weeks. To test its general suction, I scattered loose tea and lentils over hard floor and carpet to simulate how it would handle dust and larger debris and see how many passes it would take to suction them up. I also scattered both of these items along the edge of the room to see how well the Shark would maintain suction at the edges.
On top of this, I used it to clean my whole house several times, as well as trying it out in a few specific scenarios. I tested how well it sucked up shed fur from my pet cat, as well as trying its HairPro Self-Cleaning Pet Power brush on upholstery and on the stairs to see how it removed built up hair from soft furnishings. Finally, I used a sound level meter to record how loud it was in use, recording its max volume in both upright mode and during self cleaning.
I’ve been testing tech and gadgets for around 10 years, as well as editing reviews of smart home gear and appliances. When it comes to first-hand experience, I’ve tested an array of small appliances for TechRadar, including fans and coffee machines. You’ll also be pleased to hear I’m no stranger to vacuuming — otherwise, after 20 years of adulthood, the quantity of dust in my home would be approaching the level of an Egyptian tomb.

articles.title: Las mariposas tienen un truco oculto en sus alas para escapar de los depredadores: engañar a su cerebro
articles.text:
Una de las grandes preguntas que podemos tener en la cabeza está precisamente en por qué las mariposas cuentan con deslumbrantes patrones geométricos y colores en sus alas. La explicación convencional se dividía casi siempre entre el camuflaje para pasar desapercibidas en el entorno o el aposematismo, la estrategia visual mediante la cual tonos estridentes advierten a los depredadores de la presencia de toxinas desagradables.
Una respuesta. Para tratar de entender qué es lo que ocurre, un estudio publicado en Nature demostró que ciertas características anatómicas y cromáticas no buscan ocultar al insecto, sino distorsionar el cálculo de velocidad y trayectoria que realiza el cerebro del cazador cuando la mariposa está en movimiento.
Cómo lo vieron. Para poner a prueba la hipótesis del engaño dinámico, los investigadores desarrollaron una simulación con ordenador en la que recrearon 757 formas de alas pertenecientes a 397 especies de mariposas europeas. Una vez montado este sistema, se reclutó a un centenar de voluntarios que asumieron el rol de "depredadores", y por tanto su misión era capturar las mariposas en movimiento con pantallas táctiles.
En paralelo, los científicos diseñaron una simulación evolutiva que dejó al algoritmo actuar libremente. El sistema hizo evolucionar más de 50.000 patrones de alas artificiales, seleccionando de forma automatizada aquellos diseños que generaban el mayor nivel de error y confusión en los ataques de los participantes.
El resultado. Una vez terminado el experimento, se vio que los patrones óptimos generados de manera abstracta por el ordenador terminaron coincidiendo con las especies reales que hay en la naturaleza. Y el verdadero truco parece estar en las franjas verticales contrastadas, las bandas únicas transversales y las extensiones en forma de cola en las alas posteriores.
Hay matices. El sistema visual de los depredadores no es el mismo en todas las especies, sino que hay cambios importantes. Por ejemplo, las aves procesan la imagen a una velocidad concreta, pero otros depredadores de las mariposas, como las libélulas, cuentan con una resolución mucho más rápida.
En estos insectos cazadores, capaces de procesar un número muy superior de fotogramas por segundo, la ilusión óptica creada por el aleteo podría no surtir efecto, lo que explica por qué capturan mariposas en pleno vuelo con un porcentaje de éxito muy elevado. Es por ello que este sistema de defensa con unas alas que enamoran a cualquiera puede no ser perfecto para todos los depredadores.

Imágenes | Frederica Black

articles.title: Angel One becomes India's second-largest broker by active clients
articles.text:
Angel One becomes India's second-largest broker by active clients
The active client base of Angel One for October was 69.98 lakh which was an addition of 2.43 lakh for the month. Zerodha now is in the third spot.
Financial Services firm Angel One has become the country's second-largest stockbroker in terms of active clients, with 69.98 lakh investors on the National Stock Exchange at the end of October, according to the exchange's latest data.
With an active client base of 69.98 lakh, the brokerage now accounts for 14.97% of 4.67 crore active clients across all brokers on the exchange.
The firm added 2.43 lakh net active clients on NSE in October alone.
Its overall client base reached 4.06 crore at the end of October, up 17.4% year-on-year. The company crossed the 4-crore mark during the month after adding nearly 15 lakh clients in the July-September quarter.
Trading activity also picked up in October, with average daily orders rising 19.6% month-on-month to 69.7 lakh. Gross client additions stood at 6.6 lakh, the highest in nine months.
In terms of the number one position, Groww retained its spot with 1.37 crore active clients for the month of October. It also added the highest number of clients at 3.04 lakh during the month and also Groww’s market share was 29.43%.
Bengaluru headquartered Zerodha slipped to third position with overall 67.59 lakh active clients for the month of October which was down by 32,435 from 67.91 lakh in September. This resulted in Zerodha’s market share slipping to 14.46%.
The growth in client numbers of Angel One came alongside an improvement in financial performance.
Angel One's consolidated revenue from operations rose 18.7% year-on-year to Rs 1,427 crore, and net profit grew 58.2% to Rs 335 crore.
Its wealth management assets under management stood at Rs 16,000 crore at the end of the quarter, up 19.1 per cent sequentially.

articles.title: Nvidia will investigate CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with possible Chinese spy | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Nvidia’s board of directors announced Sunday that it’s launching an independent investigation following reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation.
Nvidia also published a message that Huang sent to the company admitting that he had an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed (though he didn’t mention her by name). A memo circulating among U.S. policymakers earlier this year claimed that Alice Huang had been recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia’s CEO.
“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Jensen Huang wrote. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”
Huang added that he’d “fallen short” of his responsibility to the company.
“To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me,” he said.
As the AI race between the United States and China heats up, chips, especially Nvidia’s chips, have been a major focus. Huang also seems to have a close relationship with President Donald Trump, who’s been a cheerleader of the AI (or “superintelligence”) industry.
In its announcement, Nvidia’s board said that it has “no reason to believe” that either national security or company secrets were compromised. It also said that Huang “fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it,” and that the board has “confidence in Jensen and his leadership team.”
The investigation will be conducted by independent directors working with outside legal counsel.
In response to earlier reports about the CEO’s relationship with Alice Huang, Nvidia had said that the pair’s interactions were “not unusual,” and that the company does not share classified information with customers.
Other companies involved in the AI boom have warned employees to be wary of possible spies, including those offering sex or romance.

articles.title: Meta vous laisse ajouter vos propres outils à son application Muse en les décrivant à son IA
articles.text:
Pour obtenir un suivi de vos cadeaux de Noël ou un planning de mariage dans Muse, l’agent IA de Meta, il vous suffit de lui expliquer, dans la conversation, de quel outil vous avez besoin. Muse le fabrique, puis le tient à jour tout seul à partir des services que vous lui avez connectés.
La nouvelle fonction s’appelle Spaces, et vous pourrez la trouver dans la barre latérale de Muse, que Meta propose pour l'instant aux États-Unis et au Canada. Chaque espace est un onglet consacré à un seul projet, un voyage en famille ou des travaux de bricolage par exemple. Comme l’explique Mark Zuckerberg sur X, « dites à Muse ce qu’il vous faut et il le construit ». Le patron de Meta raconte s’être ainsi fabriqué un jeu autour du barbecue et un tableau de bord pour piloter sa maison, rien qu’en les demandant à son agent.
Muse construit chaque espace à partir de votre description
« Décrivez une idée dans la conversation, et Muse vous construit un espace, qu’il s’agisse d’un outil de suivi, d’un planning ou d’un tableau de projet », souligne Meta dans son annonce. Dans les exemples de l’entreprise, Muse relève dans les courriels de l’école les sorties et les réunions de vos enfants, puis il les inscrit dans votre agenda. Pour un mariage, l’agent rassemble les réponses des invités et les factures des prestataires.
Meta pense aussi aux petites structures. Si vous êtes à votre compte, Muse peut regrouper vos projets et vos factures dans un seul onglet. Et si vous tenez une boutique, il suit pour vous les nouvelles commandes et les messages de vos clients.
Une fois l’espace créé, vous pouvez demander à Muse d’ajouter une rubrique oubliée ou de changer l’apparence de l’outil. Vous gardez la main sur le contenu, avec la possibilité de cocher des éléments à la main ou d’ajouter vos notes.
Muse actualise ensuite chaque espace en arrière-plan, à partir des applications que vous lui avez connectées. Selon Meta, une nouvelle date de concert de votre artiste préféré ou une baisse de prix sur un article de votre liste vous parvient alors sans que vous ayez besoin de relancer l’agent.
Meta réserve Spaces aux pays où Muse est disponible
Meta a lancé Spaces au lendemain de Muse Voice, avec lequel vous pouvez parler à votre agent en appel vidéo et lui donner vos ordres à la voix. L’entreprise multiplie les nouveautés depuis le succès de Muse, sorti le 8 septembre. Lors de la présentation des résultats trimestriels d’octobre, Mark Zuckerberg annonçait 10 millions d’utilisateurs aux États-Unis et au Canada, moins de deux mois après le lancement.
Spaces est ouvert dans tous les pays où Muse est disponible, et aucun pays de l’Union européenne ne fait partie de la liste. Meta n’a donné aucune date de sortie pour la France, et l’Europe devra encore patienter avant de profiter de l’agent.
Pour travailler à votre place, Muse demande l’accès à vos e-mails, à votre agenda et parfois à vos moyens de paiement. Meta fait tourner chaque agent sur une machine virtuelle isolée dans le cloud, où un second agent maison, Sentinel, doit valider tout envoi de données vers l’extérieur. L’entreprise reconnaît malgré tout que Muse peut encore commettre des erreurs. Et pour remplir le tableau de bord scolaire imaginé par Meta, Muse doit parcourir chaque courriel envoyé par l’école de vos enfants.
- Tâches complètes de bout en bout
- Contrôles d’accès très détaillés
- Travail autonome en arrière-plan

articles.title: Weltrekord: E-Hypercar von BYD fährt über 500 km/h schnell
articles.text:
Weltrekord für E-Hypercar von BYD: Yangwang U9 Xtreme fährt über 500 km/h schnell
Schon bisher galt das E-Hypercar Yangwang U9 Xtreme des chinesischen Autokonzerns BYD als schnellstes Serienfahrzeug der Welt. Bei Testfahrten in Deutschland im Herbst 2025 erreichte das Elektrofahrzeug eine Höchstgeschwindigkeit von 496 Kilometern pro Stunde.
Erstes Auto knackt 500-km/h-Marke
Damit hatte das BYD-Hypercar den Bugatti Chiron Supersport 300 Plus abgelöst, der mit 490 Kilometern pro Stunde aber der schnellste Verbrenner der Welt bleibt. Jetzt hat der Yangwang U9 Xtreme als erstes Auto der Welt die Marke von 500 Kilometern pro Stunde geknackt.
Konkret erreichte der E-Flitzer am 1. November 2026 auf einer abgesperrten Autobahn in Abu Dhabi eine Höchstgeschwindigkeit von 503,17 Kilometern pro Stunde, wie BYD per X mitteilte. Am Steuer des 3.019 PS starken Fahrzeugs saß demnach der deutsche Langstreckenpilot Marc Basseng.
Mit dem Geschwindigkeitsrekord sicherte sich BYD gleich zwei Einträge ins Guinnessbuch der Weltrekorde, darunter den für das schnellste Serienfahrzeug. Außerdem ist das E-Hypercar damit auch das schnellste elektrische Serienfahrzeug der Welt. Beides gilt jeweils für eine Fahrt in eine Richtung.
Wie Motor1 schreibt, war der Yangwang U9 Xtreme am Tag vor dem Erreichen der Höchstgeschwindigkeit schon mit 490 Kilometern pro Stunde unterwegs gewesen. Optimierungen am Anstellwinkel des Heckflügels sowie am Reifenfülldruck und der Steuerungssoftware ermöglichten dann das erstmalige Durchbrechen der 500-km/h-Marke.
Spezielle Reifen, um Belastung standzuhalten
Neben seiner Systemleistung von gut 3.000 PS nutzt der Supersportwagen ein 1.200-Volt-Bordnetz. Als Energiespeicher kommt eine adaptierte LFP-Batterie der Blade-Bauart zum Einsatz. Der Reifenhersteller Giti Tire lieferte speziell auf das Fahrzeug abgestimmte Semi-Slick-Reifen, um den extremen Belastungen standhalten zu können.
BYD bietet den Yangwang U9 Xtreme auch zum Kauf an. Die Kleinserie ist aber auf 30 Exemplare begrenzt. Motor1 zufolge soll das erste Fahrzeug mit den Namen „Dawn Moment“ über eine Speziallackierung mit mikrometischem Goldstaub verfügen.
Yangwang U9 Xtreme kostet 2,7 Millionen Euro
Erste Kaufverträge sollen unterschrieben und die entsprechenden individuellen Konfigurationen finalisiert sein. Das E-Hypercar kostet in China über 20 Millionen Yuan, was umgerechnet rund 2,7 Millionen Euro entspricht.

articles.title: Lista de los 10 videos en YouTube que son tendencia en Chile este día
articles.text:
Aunque redes sociales como Facebook e Instagram están apostando cada vez más por los videos, lo cierto es que YouTube sigue siendo el rey al ser la segunda página más visitada en el mundo sólo por detrás del buscador Google.
YouTube tiene presencia en 104 países y está disponible en 80 idiomas, por lo que no sorprende que en dicha plataforma puedas encontrar un video de BTS, pasando por videos de terror hasta llegar a contenido educativo sobre cómo resolver una ecuación.
La plataforma estadounidense, surgida en el año 2005, se ha convertido en la biblioteca digital de videos más grande del mundo y prueba de ello es que a ella se suben más de 500 horas de contenido cada minuto, al día son vistos 5 mil millones de videos y las ganancias se estiman en 15 mil millones de dólares al trimestre.
Ante estas cifras podría ser un tanto difícil perderse las novedades o los clips que están siendo los más populares, es por eso que YouTube cuenta desde 2018 con diversas listas en donde se pueden consultar los artistas más escuchados, los videos más vistos y cuáles son las tendencias del día en tiempo real.
Acá el listado de los 10 nuevos videos que están en tendencia
1. LA PLAYAArtista/canal: Katteyes, Swift 047, Benja Valencia y SINAKA
2. Ya Estoy LlegandoArtista/canal: Mati Bomba, Boy Wonder CF, Divino y Bayron Fire
3. EL QUE AVISA NO TRAICIONAArtista/canal: Drakomafia, Milan Didier, JulianoChieff y bayriton
4. UH LA LÁ!Artista/canal: Jere Klein, Corredor y Space Records
5. JAIRO VERA - PKTD (Video oficial) Prod. Ag DaddyArtista/canal: Jairo Vera TV
6. POKITOArtista/canal: Daddy Yankee
7. Kidd Voodoo, Macha y El Bloque Depresivo - VOLVER A COMENZAR (Video Oficial)Artista/canal: Kidd Voodoo
8. LAJA x ANUEL AA - TUSSI (Video Oficial)Artista/canal: LAJA
9. LA PLAYAArtista/canal: Benja Valencia, Katteyes, SINAKA y Swift 047
10. SudacaArtista/canal: DUKI, Pablo Chill-E y Lucho SSJ
El éxito de YouTube
YouTube vio la luz en febrero de 2005, cuando tres antiguos empleados de la compañía de Paypal ―Chad Hurley, Steve Chen y Jawed Karim― se unieron y la crearon luego de que experimentaran dificultades para compartir entre sí un par de videos tras asistir a una fiesta.
El dominio fue activado el 14 de febrero de 2005 y casi un mes después, el 23 de abril, fue cargado el primer clip a la plataforma que llevaba por nombre “Me at the Zoo”. Fue cuestión de tiempo para que todo el mundo comenzara a cargar contenido y a compartir los enlaces a través de otras redes sociales como MySpace.
Una de las grandes empresas que vio el potencial de YouTube fue la marca Nike, que subió una publicidad protagonizada por Ronaldinho, lo que hizo que otras grandes compañías voltearan a ver a YouTube y se sintieran atraídas.
Tal fue la gran acogida de los internautas por YouTube que para diciembre de 2005 la plataforma pasó de las 50 millones de visitas al día a 250 millones de visualizaciones luego de que un canal subiera el clip musical Lazy Sunday, transmitido originalmente por Saturday Night Live.
Para el año siguiente, en el 2006, el sitio fue comparado por el gigante del internet, Google, por un valor de 1650 millones de dólares. En ese entonces eran visualizados 100 millones de videos al día y 65 mil clips se añadían a diario. También firmaron acuerdos con disqueras para poder reproducir videos musicales.
YouTube: entre la cultura popular y la política
Desde que fue puesto en marcha, YouTube fue un sitio que llegó a hacer una revolución no sólo en internet, sino también en la forma en la que los usuarios miran contenido. Muestra de ello el reconocimiento que la revista Time le otorgó en noviembre del 2006 al ser nombrado el “Invento del Año”.
Convertido en el mejor medio de difusión, el gozar de tanta popularidad también ha metido a sus dueños en aprietos como cuando albergar peleas escolares o en donde hay bullying, clips relacionados al terrorismo, narcotráfico u otros temas considerados delicados por su contenido íntimo o por mostrar delitos como asesinatos y más.
Para Estados Unidos uno de los temas más delicados es el de los tiroteos escolares, por lo que YouTube ha estado más de una vez en el ojo del huracán por alojar contenido filmado por los atacantes, como fue el caso de la masacre de Virginia Tech, cuando Cho Seung-Hui, el atacante, subió previamente a los hechos un discurso.
Más recientemente, tras el surgimiento de la pandemia del coronavirus, también ha surgido inquietud sobre cómo la plataforma permite la monetización de contenido que puede ser engañoso y riesgoso para la población.
Aunque no todo es malo, pues a través de dicha plataforma muchas personas han podido ser reconocidas por su talento, como fue el caso de Susan Boyle, quien participó en el programa Britain’s Got Talent cuyo extracto subido a YouTube logró que la mujer pasara a ser una completa desconocida a una de las personas más viralizadas, famosas y aclamadas del internet.

articles.title: Employed job seekers are shunning companies which use AI interviews — and I don't blame them
articles.text:
Employed job seekers are shunning companies which use AI interviews — and I don't blame them
Impersonal AI interviewers putting off candidates
- AI interviews are discouraging people from fully participating in the job application process
- Jobseekers who are already employed are less likely to accept an AI interview
- 58% of people who attended an AI interview despite reservations would refuse if other jobs were lined up
Automated interviews are becoming a turn-off for jobseekers, particularly if they already have a job, new research has revealed.
A survey from Use.AI of people looking for work in the UK, US, Canada, European Union, and Latin America found nearly a third (29%) of people already in work had withdrawn from a hiring process that involved an AI interview.
Meanwhile, just 14% of those without work withdrew, demonstrating the importance of finding work when unemployed.
Available for consideration
Intriguingly, while the specific figures concerning the 6731 survey subjects differ across all regions, the pattern of a split between those already employed and those who are not is repeated.
Use.AI’s findings indicate that a candidate’s willingness to participate in an AI interview can depend on several factors, including financial security and what other options the jobseeker already has.
Most of the jobs you see advertised today have AI filtering to hopefully determine the best candidates. The businesses going one step beyond this and detaching themselves from the interview process seem to be making a mistake.
“Employers spend considerable effort checking whether their screening systems evaluate candidates fairly. They should be equally interested in who decides to enter those systems in the first place,” said Matthew Freire, Managing Director of Use.AI.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
“Offering applicants an alternative route to a human interviewer would allow companies to examine whether the format itself is influencing who remains available for consideration.”
Replacing hiring experts and people who know the job as interviewers may have saved time and money in the short-term. But if no one wants to be hired by a company that relies on AI interviews, then productivity is lost, and along with it, profit.
Automated Recruitment
Searching for a new job increasingly requires the submission of a resume for screening. Those CVs or applications might then find their way to a human, and a call may be scheduled. But many companies are relying on in-house and third party AI interviewers. It isn’t only potential employers, either – some recruitment agencies are staffed by AI interviewers, too.
All of this makes the job application process increasingly challenging, particularly if you’re someone who relies heavily on body language and facial signals. Succeeding in an interview often means building a rapport with the people on the other side of the table or display, and this is something that simply isn’t possible when the person asking the questions isn’t a person at all.
The graphical representation of a programmed LLM may appear smart and attractive, and they have the questions read to ask. But it is ultimately an elaborate piece of form-filling that doesn't demonstrate a person's ability to establish instant rapport and translate that into working relationships.

He currently heads up the team at smart home website Matter Alpha, and writes about retro gaming at Gaming Retro.
