articles.title: Workflow, AI, health: test your business creativity with Edition 257 of our weekly quiz!
articles.text:
Workflow, AI, health: test your business creativity with Edition 257 of our weekly quiz!
This insightful feature from YourStory tests and strengthens your business acumen! Here are 5 questions to kick off this 257th quiz. Ready?
Lateral Sparks, the weekly quiz from YourStory, tests your domain knowledge, business acumen, and lateral thinking skills (see the previous edition here). In this 257th edition of the quiz, we present issues tackled by real-life entrepreneurs in their startup journeys.
What would you do if you were in their shoes? At the end of the quiz, you will find out what the entrepreneurs and innovators themselves actually did. Would you do things differently?
Check out YourStory’s Book Review section as well, with takeaways from over 355 titles on creativity and entrepreneurship, and our weekend PhotoSparks section on creativity in the arts.
Q1: Healthcare
The healthcare system is generally built to treat illness, not to find it early. Where are the entrepreneurial opportunities in preventive care at scale?
Q2: Elder care
Senior citizens today are unwilling to let age define how they live, and are looking for more quality of lifestyle. Where is the business opportunity here?
Q3: Recycling
Efficient recycling of components in used objects can be complex in terms of determining what is inside, how much material can be recovered, and what it will cost to process. How can efficiency be improved here?
Q4: Social insights
Social media is a key discovery and evaluation channel for consumers, but brands don’t leverage these insights well. What can be done to deepen and apply business signals here?
Q5: Construction
Cost overruns, project delays, and disconnected processes remain major challenges in the construction industry. How can technology help here?
Answers!
Congratulations on having come this far! But there’s more to come – answers to these five questions (below), as well as links to articles with more details on the entrepreneurs’ solutions. Happy reading, happy learning – and happy creating!
A1: Healthcare
Founded by Shashank ND, Arpit Garg, and Anshul Khandelwal, healthtech startup Cent is building a vertically integrated preventive health platform. It combines customised hardware, AI-driven radiology, and bioinformatics.
It has reportedly completed 10,000 preventive whole-body scans in three cities since launch, and is targeting 10 million scans by 2035. Read more here about its disease detection capabilities, and its recent fundraise from Blume Ventures and South Park Commons.
A2: Elder care
Founded by Sharad Gadsing, Cradle Of Life focuses on offering seniors four fundamental human aspirations: freedom, purpose, health, and happiness. It enables seniors to learn, contribute and pursue what matters personally.
In terms of design, the residential facilities include a central balcony that extends to every room, layouts with more usable area, and safety through age-friendly furniture. Read more here about its other offerings in healthcare, emergency response, wellness, and community engagement.
A3: Recycling
Attero is an e-waste and battery recycling company that uses AI to speed up decisions across thousands of appliances, suppliers and locations. It processes 200,000 metric tonnes of e-waste and 10,000 metric tonnes of lithium-ion batteries annually, according to Ayush Agarwal, Head of Product.
Its pricing engine combines material intelligence with market intelligence to calculate what the material should cost in a particular market. Read more here about its AI-powered compliance engine that checks documents, reconciles information across records, and flags exceptions.
A4: Social insights
“Brands today are drowning in signals and starved of action,” explains J Venkat, Co-founder of Live2.ai. It monitors conversations across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Reddit, X, and review websites.
It integrates trend analysis, influencer-content audits, campaign publishing, and performance measurement for ecommerce. Read more here about how it serves more than 200 brands across the US, Europe and Southeast Asia.
A5: Construction
Founded by Saurav Bhaik and Ankit Sinha, Tagbin has developed an AI-powered product that integrates architectural drawings, mechanical systems, and project costing. The integrated workflow can be controlled through natural-language prompts.
The platform generates building models, incorporates applicable regulations, and creates construction schedules. Read more here about how it also takes soil-bearing strength and the water table into account while generating foundations and excavation plans.
YourStory has also published the pocketbook ‘Proverbs and Quotes for Entrepreneurs: A World of Inspiration for Startups’ as a creative and motivational guide for innovators.

articles.title: If Snap's Specs are still ridiculously expensive, they're also a lot more comfortable than they used to be | TechCrunch
articles.text:
When I tried a prototype of Snap’s Specs at CES in Las Vegas earlier this year, the experience left something to be desired. The company’s AR glasses — which the company calls a “new kind of computer” — were heavy (they weighed around 8 ounces) and fit rather uncomfortably on my face. The device was also hot, and made my face feel tingly — a common side-effect of smart glasses where massive computing is happening under the hood.
Fast forward to late October, when I met back up with the Snap team at a Four Seasons in downtown San Francisco. By this time, the company had debuted Specs publicly during an event with CEO Evan Spiegel, and pre-orders of the company’s long-gestating headset were already underway.
What I can say is this: Specs has improved the form factor significantly since my first brush with the device. The glasses now weigh nearly half of what the previous version did, slimming down to 132 grams, or approximately 4.6 ounces. They were quite comfortable and, during the hour-ish that I demo-ed the device, it did not heat up like the previous version had.
Specs now comes in two sizes — 47mm and 52mm. The purpose here is purely to accommodate different head sizes, ensuring the glasses fit snugly on whoever’s face happens to be wearing them. They also now come equipped with spring hinges, which make the device more flexible and comfortable.
However, if the body of the device has improved greatly, its soul is still a work-in-progress. The glasses can be fun — but they also still seem to lack a dedicated purpose, and one struggles to imagine how, specifically, this expensive head gear ($2,200 a pop) would prove useful in a daily capacity. When I asked Snap staff what the device was really for — fun and games or productivity — the answer was vague. The device attempts to be a bunch of things at once and, in the process, ends up feeling a little rudderless.
I have racked my brain to come up with some daily use-cases for Specs. Some of the things I came up with were:
- Watching TV or movies while you’re on a train or some other form of public transportation. There are places where you just have to hang out for awhile and, not infrequently, one way to pass the time is streaming. Specs provides a much more immersive form of mobile entertainment than simply watching a video on your cell phone. The device’s integrations with HBO Max and YouTube make it an appealing entertainment option for users who are in-transit.
- Reading. Because of the immersive nature of Snap’s headset, I feel like they could be a good option for reading while traveling. When you’re reading with Specs, it feels like you’re locked into whatever text you happen to be looking at. It weirdly helped me focus. An integration for newspapers or Kindle could make the glasses a good way to read while you’re mobile (I’m envisioning the ideal setting being on a plane, train, or the back of a car).
- Taking easily shareable weird videos. Like many of Meta’s smart glasses, Specs allows users to take photographs and videos, which is an odd but fun component of the user experience. The ability to generate GoPro-like videos and easily text them to your friends is something that I could see the casual user doing on a somewhat regular basis.
By contrast, here are some of the areas I’m still not totally sold on as Specs use-cases:
- Specs as a daily workspace and productivity tool. Snap is selling Specs as a way to work. The company claims its headset can “transform almost any location into an immersive, flexible workspace.” However, I have a really hard time imagining Specs being something that the average worker is going to want to incorporate into their workflows. It’s less convenient to strap the glasses to your head than it is to simply sit at your computer typing. What can Specs provide that a cell phone and laptop can’t? The social stigma of wearing weird, large glasses and gesticulating to operate them would also seem to be a deterrent.
- A widely used gaming device. Due to the prohibitive cost of the device (again, nearly $2200), I have a really hard time imagining that there is going to be a huge audience for Specs as a gaming device. Most Xboxes are under half the price of this device. Are the games on Specs fun? Sure, kind of. But are teenagers going to be clamoring for them come Christmas time? That I’m not so sure about.
Specs is impressive for how the Snap team has managed to integrate a variety of user experiences into one unified device. There are a lot of impressive achievements here — specifically the spatial synching tech that allows two users to see the same thing simultaneously — that, with some further development, could be deployed towards some really interesting use cases.
The bottom line is that Snap’s device can continue to grow and transform as the company iterates. It’s an interesting product that — like a lot of its peers — doesn’t necessarily seem to have a clear purpose but, in time, could become many things.
What the device currently offers, however, may not be compelling enough to encourage people to shell out the cash that Snap is asking for.

articles.title: Resulta que el "rey" que llevó a Roma hasta Britania era una mujer: la pista estaba en sus monedas
articles.text:
En el año 43 d.C., el Imperio Romano invadió Britania, si bien desde hace poco sabemos que su "conquista" había empezado antes. El historiador Dion Casio escribió en el siglo III que Verica, gobernante de los atrebates en el sur de Britania y con alianzas con Roma, fue "expulsado" y huyó. Esa huida sirvió como pretexto y facilitó que Claudio invadiera la isla. Hasta ahora, creíamos que Verica, descendiente del rey Commio, era un hombre. Miles Russell, arqueólogo y profesor de la Universidad de Bournemouth, defiende que era una mujer.
El rey era en realidad una reina. El arqueólogo británico expone en Current Archaeology y en su próximo libro "Caratacus: Great king of Britain" que Verica fue reina y lo hace basándose en tres razones: su nombre termina en "a", algo común en los nombres femeninos de la época y que de hecho observamos en las reinas Cartimandua de los Brigantes (en Yorkshire) y de Boudica de los Icenos (en Norfolk).
Buena parte del argumento está en las monedas acuñadas en su nombre y encontradas en Hampshire y Sussex. El segundo motivo es que la palabra «rex» que aparece en ellas es un título de género neutro, de modo que no impide que fuera una mujer. El tercero es la figura representada: "Mientras que otros líderes británicos de la Edad del Hierro que acuñaron monedas representan a guerreros claramente masculinos, Verica es representada como una figura esbelta, femenina y con el pecho descubierto, montada a caballo", explica el arqueólogo.
Las monedas como único texto escrito. Como casi no hay textos escritos de la Britania de la Edad del Hierro, resulta que las monedas son prácticamente el único testimonio escrito que ha aguantado esos 2.000 años. En las monedas aparece asimismo "COMF", que se interpretaban como hijo de Commio, pero que también podría significar hija.
La oportunidad de Claudio. Para Claudio, un emperador del que historiadores romanos como Dion Casio se burlaban presentándolo como débil y fácilmente influenciable por sus esposas, esta invasión fue la ocasión perfecta para demostrar su valía militar. Russell sostiene que en el relato de la conquista de Dion Casio la campaña nace de los susurros de una "femme fatale bárbara", lo que encaja con la imagen de un Claudio manipulable y con que Verica fuera mujer.
Por qué importa. ¿Por qué dar por hecho entonces desde el principio que Verica era un hombre? Russell explica que suele asumirse así «debido a la mentalidad patriarcal de los historiadores clásicos del siglo XIX», como declara para EurekAlert. Y que su papel fue fundamental para la relación especial entre Gran Bretaña y Roma de principios del siglo I d. C. Si Russell lleva razón, la Britania prerromana habría tenido al menos tres líderes políticas de primera línea, todas del siglo I d. C. Además, el arqueólogo considera a Verica la más significativa de las tres. Que usara el término rex en las monedas demuestra, según el arqueólogo, que Verica gobernaba con la plena autorización del emperador.
La teoría de Miles Russell encaja además con un estudio de ADN en el que se analizó más de 50 genomas de cementerios de Dorset, territorio de los durotriges y no de los atrebates y llegó a una conclusión: la mayoría de los individuos descendía de una misma antepasada por línea materna, y los datos apuntan a una sociedad matrilineal y matrilocal en la que los maridos se mudaban a vivir con la comunidad de sus esposas.

YouTube ha adquirido una importancia sin precedentes en el mundo moderno y en su momento se convirtió en un fenómeno que llegó a revolucionar la forma en que se consume el contenido audiovisual.
Antes de su existencia el acceso a este tipo de clips estaba limitado a canales de televisión tradicionales y producciones de gran presupuesto, sin embargo, YouTube ha permitido que cualquier persona con una cámara y una conexión a internet pueda hacer y compartir sus propios clips, lo que ha beneficiado a la aparición de una amplia cantidad de canales que brindan desde contenido educativo hasta de entretenimiento.
La plataforma también ha funcionado como un trampolín para artistas emergentes, músicos, comediantes y cineastas independientes, quienes han encontrado en YouTube una audiencia global y la posibilidad de obtener reconocimiento sin pasar por los canales tradicionales de la industria del entretenimiento.
YouTube tiene presencia en 104 países y está disponible en 80 idiomas, lo que la ha llevado a convertirse en la biblioteca digital de videos más grande y prueba de ello es que a ella se suben más de 500 horas de contenido cada minuto, al día son vistos 5 mil millones de videos y las ganancias se estiman en 15 mil millones de dólares al trimestre.
Ante estas cifras podría ser un tanto difícil perderse las novedades o los clips que están siendo los más populares, es por eso que YouTube cuenta desde 2018 con diversas listas en donde se pueden consultar los artistas más escuchados, los videos más vistos y cuáles son las tendencias del día en tiempo real.

Los inicios de YouTube
YouTube vio la luz en febrero de 2005, cuando tres antiguos empleados de la compañía de Paypal ―Chad Hurley, Steve Chen y Jawed Karim― se unieron y la crearon luego de que experimentaran dificultades para compartir entre sí un par de videos tras asistir a una fiesta.
El dominio fue activado el 14 de febrero de 2005 y casi un mes después, el 23 de abril, fue cargado el primer video a la plataforma que llevaba por nombre “Me at the Zoo”. Fue cuestión de tiempo para que todo el mundo comenzara a cargar contenido y a compartir los enlaces a través de otras redes sociales como MySpace.
Una de las grandes empresas que vio el potencial de YouTube fue la marca Nike, que subió una publicidad protagonizada por Ronaldinho, lo que hizo que otras grandes compañías voltearan a ver a YouTube y se sintieran atraídas.
Tal fue la gran acogida de los internautas por YouTube que para diciembre de 2005 la plataforma pasó de las 50 millones de visitas al día a 250 millones de visualizaciones luego de que un canal subiera el clip musical Lazy Sunday, transmitido originalmente por Saturday Night Live.
Para el año siguiente, en el 2006, el sitio fue comparado por el gigante del internet, Google, por un valor de 1650 millones de dólares. En ese entonces eran visualizados 100 millones de videos al día y 65 mil clips se añadían a diario. También firmaron acuerdos con disqueras para poder reproducir videos musicales.
El impacto de YouTube
Desde que fue puesto en marcha, YouTube fue un sitio que llegó a hacer una revolución no sólo en internet, sino también en la forma en la que los usuarios miran contenido. Muestra de ello el reconocimiento que la revista Time le otorgó en noviembre del 2006 al ser nombrado el “Invento del Año”.
Convertido en el mejor medio de difusión, el gozar de tanta popularidad también ha metido a sus dueños en aprietos como cuando albergar peleas escolares o en donde hay bullying, clips relacionados al terrorismo, narcotráfico u otros temas considerados delicados por su contenido íntimo o por mostrar delitos como asesinatos y más.
Para Estados Unidos uno de los temas más delicados es el de los tiroteos escolares, por lo que YouTube ha estado más de una vez en el ojo del huracán por alojar contenido filmado por los atacantes, como fue el caso de la masacre de Virginia Tech, cuando Cho Seung-Hui, el atacante, subió previamente a los hechos un discurso.
Más recientemente, tras el surgimiento de la pandemia del coronavirus, también ha surgido inquietud sobre cómo la plataforma permite la monetización de contenido que puede ser engañoso y riesgoso para la población.
Aunque no todo es malo, pues a través de dicha plataforma muchas personas han podido ser reconocidas por su talento, como fue el caso de Susan Boyle, quien participó en el programa Britain’s Got Talent cuyo extracto subido a YouTube logró que la mujer pasara a ser una completa desconocida a una de las personas más viralizadas, famosas y aclamadas del internet.

articles.title: Quarante ans après Tchernobyl, des scientifiques découvrent que des particules radioactives du réacteur sont restées presque intactes malgré les décennies
articles.text:
Quarante ans après Tchernobyl, des scientifiques découvrent que des particules radioactives du réacteur sont restées presque intactes malgré les décennies
Quarante ans après la catastrophe de Tchernobyl, les scientifiques se penchent encore sur la catastrophe nucléaire. Des chercheurs ont analysé six particules radioactives expulsées du réacteur numéro 4 et leur découverte est pour le moins surprenante.
Les scientifiques se sont donc penchés sur six particules radioactives expulsées du réacteur numéro 4. Leur découverte, c'est que le combustible nucléaire a gardé une grande partie de sa structure d'origine avec des poussières de seulement 8 à 50 micromètres. En 2026, on trouve donc toujours ces fragments radioactifs et certains débris ont beaucoup moins changé qu'on ne l'attendait.
Des fragments radioactifs projetés lors de l'explosion
Rappelons que c'est le 26 avril 1986 que le réacteur numéro 4 a explosé lors d'un test de sécurité. L'incendie du graphite a duré dix jours et des fragments de combustible furent projetés autour de la centrale de Tchernobyl.
Il s'agit de ce que les chercheurs appellent des "particules chaudes", dont certaines ressemblent encore au dioxyde d'uranium utilisé comme combustible. Mais ce n'est pas tout puisque d'autres ont fusionné avec le zirconium qui entourait le combustible et le feu a transformé une partie du combustible en oxydes d'uranium plus fragiles.
Les chercheurs souhaitaient découvrir pourquoi ces débris ne se dégradent pas tous à la même vitesse, puisque leur composition change fortement selon ce qui leur est arrivé dans le réacteur.
Les scientifiques ont isolé six particules de deux sites ukrainiens puis les ont envoyées à Grenoble sous plusieurs couches de protection. Christoph Hennig, cristallographe au Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf, explique : "Nous avons mesuré chaque particule sous 2 000 angles différents".
La méthode passe par des rayons X qui montrent l'organisation des atomes dans un matériau. Les scientifiques ont reconstruit la structure interne de chaque fragment sans le détruire pour distinguer les différentes formes d'oxyde d'uranium cachées dans ces poussières.
Le combustible nucléaire a étonnamment peu changé
La surprise, c'est le combustible lui-même puisque sa structure cristalline a très peu évolué après quatre décennies dans l'environnement. Ce sont donc plusieurs particules qui ont gardé enfermés les produits radioactifs dans leur structure au lieu de les relâcher rapidement dans les sols et les eaux.
Une stabilité qui limite donc leur dispersion. Les débris les plus persistants libéreront leurs radionucléides plus tard. Tobias Weissenborn, physicien à l'université Leibniz de Hanovre, rappelle que "chaque particule possède une structure différente".
À noter que résultat n'est pas une règle générale pour toute la zone de Tchernobyl puisque l'étude n'a porté que sur six fragments seulement. Mais la découverte prolonge plusieurs décennies de recherche. En 1995, des travaux avaient déjà envisagé que la structure interne de certaines particules bloque la migration des radionucléides. En 2004, une autre étude a montré que des microchampignons attaquaient des particules riches en graphite.
Désormais, les chercheurs étudient des phases transuraniques bien plus radioactives pour mieux anticiper leur évolution et améliorer la gestion des déchets de Tchernobyl.

articles.title: Vous en doutiez ? Lisa Su l'affirme : « AMD est désormais une entreprise d’abord tournée vers les data centers »
articles.text:
Après Intel, c'est au tour d'AMD d'affirmer officiellement ce que nous avions déjà tous remarqué : le grand public et le gaming sont passés au second plan dans la stratégie du groupe.
L'explosion des besoins de l'intelligence artificielle, vous connaissez. Toutes les entreprises du secteur informatique se sont tournées vers cette révolution IA, mais toutes ne l'ont pas exprimée aussi clairement que Lisa Su, la patronne du groupe américain AMD.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Les centres de données, moteur de croissance d'AMD
Au cours d'un entretien accordé à Yahoo Finance et relayé par nos confrères du site VideoCardz, Lisa Su, PDG d'AMD, a résumé l'évolution que représente l'intelligence artificielle. par une déclaration on ne peut plus claire.
« Nous sommes une entreprise axée sur les centres de données ; c’est notre profil, et les entreprises ont besoin de plus de puissance de calcul pour faire fonctionner toutes ces applications. »
Un positionnement qui intervient seulement quelques jours après la publication des résultats financiers du troisième trimestre 2026, lesquels font ressortir de manière évidente la montée en puissance de l'activité intelligence artificielle et centre de données. Lisa Su explique cette réorientation stratégique d'AMD par l'accélération de l'adoption de l'IA. Le groupe ne fait que répondre à cette demande, cherche à l'accompagner en augmentant ses capacités de production et d'approvisionnement pour ce type de clients.
Au troisième trimestre 2026, AMD a enregistré des revenus de 8,55 milliards de dollars pour le seul secteur des centres de données. Cela correspond à 64 % de son chiffre d'affaires total de 13,38 milliards de dollars. Près des deux tiers de l'activité du groupe sont donc liés à l'IA et aux serveurs associés. Lisa Su se veut d'ailleurs optimiste pour l'avenir et elle annonce déjà une progression de 50 % de ses revenus liés à ces centres de données entre les troisième et quatrième trimestres fiscaux 2026. Mieux, en 2027, c'est carrément un doublement de l'activité qui est escompté… si la demande suit, bien sûr.
Le jeu vidéo et le grand public au second plan ?
Une réorientation stratégique qu'AMD n'est donc pas seul à réaliser. Depuis déjà plusieurs années, on voit – chez NVIDIA – la part grandissante que prennent les centres de données, par rapport au gaming notamment.
Tout récemment, Intel a également annoncé une réorientation de sa production de processeurs afin de se tourner davantage vers les centres de données et, ainsi, compenser le recul du marché du PC personnel, ou grand public. Pas de mystère, l'annonce de Lisa Su intervient dans un contexte trouble pour les autres activités d'AMD. Ainsi, le segment gaming a enregistré un recul de 40 % de son chiffre d'affaires sur un an au troisième trimestre 2026.
Le gaming ne représente plus « que » 773 millions de dollars de revenus et ce n'est guère mieux pour la division regroupant les activités « client et gaming » dans leur ensemble : on parle ici d'un chiffre d'affaires de 3,72 milliards de dollars, mais d'une baisse de 8 % sur un an et, à la manière d'Intel, AMD anticipe une baisse continue – à deux chiffres – du marché du PC personnel sur l'ensemble de l'année prochaine.
À l'occasion des midterms américaines, nous avons pu remarquer une lourde chute en bourse des valeurs technologiques aux États-Unis et la crainte d'une bulle autour de l'intelligence artificielle a plus que jamais rejailli. Interrogée sur ces inquiétudes, Lisa Su a insisté sur l'importance d'une vision à plus long terme. Elle explique qu'AMD prend ses décisions d'investissements sur un horizon de trois à cinq ans sans se soucier des soubressauts postélectoraux.
L'avenir nous dira si 2027 est à nouveau marquée par une ruée vers l'intelligence artificielle ou si les investissements colossaux consentis jusqu'à présent ne vont pas se tarir. L'avenir nous dira aussi si délaisser un segment comme le grand public – qui a pourtant permis à AMD de revenir en force grâce à l'architecture de ses processeurs Ryzen – est une bonne stratégie. En attendant, l'année 2026 aura été marquée par l'absence de nouvelle génération CPU Ryzen et GPU Radeon et 2027 prend un chemin similaire.
Source : VideoCardz

articles.title: GTA 6: So machst du deine PS5 oder Xbox bereit für 200 GB
articles.text:
GTA 6 kommt: So machst du deine PS5 oder Xbox bereit für das 200 GB Game
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
Am 19. November 2026 erscheint GTA 6. Fans der Reihe mussten sich lange gedulden, denn die Veröffentlichung des Vorgängers liegt mehr als 13 Jahre zurück. Während die Vorfreude steigt, machen neue Details allerdings klar, dass das Spiel die bisherige Hardware an ihre Grenzen bringen könnte – auch beim Speicherplatz. Wir erklären dir, wie groß der Download des langersehnten Spiels ausfallen könnte und mit welchen externen Festplatten du deine Konsole aufrüstest.
Externe Speicherlösungen für Playstation 5 und Xbox
Mehrere Medien, darunter Yahoo Tech, berichten, dass der Download von GTA 6 über 200 Gigabyte groß sein soll. Grund dafür könnten das aufwendige Design und das immersive Spielerlebnis sein. Rockstar Games hat den Umfang bisher zwar nicht offiziell bestätigt, aber auch frühere Titel brauchten viel Platz. So kam beispielsweise Red Dead Redemption 2 auf rund 125 Gigabyte. Der interne Speicher von Playstation- und Xbox-Konsolen ist allerdings begrenzt. Oft startet er bei einem Terabyte, die kompaktere Xbox Series S gibt es sogar mit nur 512 Gigabyte. Der tatsächlich freie Speicher fällt noch geringer aus, weil die Konsole einen Teil für das Betriebssystem und weitere Systemfunktionen reserviert. Wenn du ein Spiel wie GTA 6 installieren willst, wird es also schnell eng.
Unter den Pioneers Picks stellen wir dir regelmäßig weitere praktische Tools und Gadgets vor.
Die gute Nachricht ist, dass du deine Konsole um eine externe Festplatte oder SSD erweitern kannst. Dabei gibt es aber einiges zu beachten. Anders als bei älteren Konsolen kannst du Spiele für die Playstation 5 nämlich nicht direkt auf einem externen USB-Speicher zocken. Der Grund: Diese bieten nicht die nötige Geschwindigkeit. Zum Spielen müssen die Games also zuerst auf den internen Speicher der Konsole kopiert werden. Eine externe Festplatte oder SSD dient bei der Playstation 5 daher eher als Archiv für Spiele, die du länger nicht gezockt hast, und schafft Platz auf der internen Festplatte.
Speichererweiterungskarten für die Xbox Series X und S
Auch bei der Xbox hängt die Nutzung eines externen Speichers von der Konsolengeneration ab. Bei älteren Modellen kannst du direkt von einer externen Festplatte oder SSD spielen. Bei der Xbox Series X und Series S geht das nicht. Eine Ausnahme bildet die externe Speichererweiterungskarte: Sie wurde in Zusammenarbeit mit Xbox entwickelt und bietet ein nahtloses Spielerlebnis, weil du hier Games direkt von der Karte starten und spielen kannst. Sie ist so konzipiert, dass sie die gleiche Speicherleistung wie die interne SSD bietet. Laut Herstellerangaben sorgt eine Übertragungsrate von 3.000 Megabyte pro Sekunde für schnelle Ladezeiten und geringe Latenzen. Du steckst die Karte auf der Rückseite der Xbox direkt in den dafür vorgesehenen Steckplatz. Das Modell von Seagate ist mit einem oder zwei Terabyte erhältlich. Bei Amazon kostet es ab 282,99 Euro.
Seagate Game Drive für Konsolenspeicher-Erweiterungen
Sony bietet selbst einige externe Speicheroptionen an, die auf die Playstation 5 optimiert sind. Eine davon ist der Game Drive von Seagate. Der Durchmesser des Geräts beträgt 2,5 Zoll. Das Design ist der Konsole angepasst – inklusive Logo. Die externe Festplatte ist mit zwei oder fünf Terabyte erhältlich und bietet somit ausreichend Platz, um ältere Spiele zu archivieren oder überall hin mitzunehmen. Du schließt sie per USB-3.0-Schnittstelle direkt an die Konsole an. Ein erneutes Herunterladen entfällt somit. Bei Amazon kostet die kleinere Variante aktuell 150,99 Euro. Das gleiche Modell gibt es auch für die Xbox mit der klassischen schwarzen Optik der Microsoft-Konsole. Es ist mit zwei, acht und 20 Terabyte verfügbar, der Preis startet bei 128,99 Euro.
- Seagate Game Drive für Playstation 5 bei Amazon*
- Seagate Game Drive für Xbox Series X und Series S bei Amazon*
Sandisk Extreme Portable SSD für die Playstation 5
Auch Sandisk bietet externen Speicher, der offiziell für die Playstation 5 lizenziert ist. Die SSD misst ebenfalls 2,5 Zoll und orientiert sich mit ihrer weißen Farbe am Design der Sony-Konsole. Laut Hersteller bietet sie eine hohe Geschwindigkeit von bis zu 1.000 Megabyte pro Sekunde, um Spiele schnell vom externen SSD-Archiv auf den internen Speicher der Playstation 5 zu übertragen. Zudem ist sie besonders robust: Sie bietet IP65-Schutz und ist fallsicher aus bis zu drei Metern Höhe. Wie die Seagate-Festplatte schließt du die SSD per USB an die Konsole an. Das Modell gibt es mit einem oder zwei Terabyte Speicherplatz. Bei Amazon kostet es ab 200,99 Euro. Laut etablierten Preisvergleichsportalen ist das aktuell das günstigste Angebot. Trotzdem kann es sich lohnen, mit dem Kauf noch etwas zu warten, denn bis vor Kurzem war die SSD schon ab 179 Euro erhältlich.
Dieser Artikel wurde ursprünglich am 02.11.2026 veröffentlicht, interessiert jedoch immer noch sehr viele unserer Leser:innen. Deshalb haben wir ihn aktualisiert und hier nochmals zur Verfügung gestellt.

articles.title: Coordinated disturbances haunt grids worldwide. Here’s how researchers solved the mystery. | TechCrunch
articles.text:
For years, mysterious electrical anomalies have been flummoxing grid managers around the world. Every 60 seconds, the frequency on the grid would drop a tiny bit.
Even weirder: The sags happened at the exact same time on power grids across countries and continents.
It was a mystery that Dirk Witthaut, a researcher at Forschungszentrum Jülich in Germany, couldn’t pass up.
Germany’s largest transmission system operator, Tennet Germany, brought the puzzle to Witthaut, and it took years of investigative and modeling work to determine the cause. From Europe to Australia, the U.S. to Malaysia, the same pattern shows up in the data.
Such frequency drops aren’t unheard of, but they are troubling. And the regularity with which they have been occurring can make the phenomenon feel even more ominous.
Balancing the grid
The grid’s orderly operation relies on the frequency being kept within a certain range. If the oscillations get get too large, or if grid operators don’t know the cause and respond improperly, they can lead to blackouts. Even if the sags don’t cause blackouts, they can damage equipment in power plants if they go unchecked, especially in hydropower turbines.
Hydropower plants have historically been a main driver of so-called ultra-low frequency oscillations (UFLOs). Every turbine vibrates, and if those vibrations occur with a certain regularity, known as the resonant frequency, they can magnify, sometimes to dangerous levels. Think of a wine glass breaking before an opera singer’s mighty pipes — that’s resonance.
So Witthaut and his team started investigating hydropower, the most obvious potential culprit. They used a computer model of a hydropower plant control system on the Scandinavian grid to test the hypothesis.
While they managed to find conditions that could generate a resonance that peaked once per minute, they couldn’t explain why it persisted for so long. Typically, resonances in mechanical systems will come and go, and so will the accompanying signal on the electrical grid. But this frequency drop kept happening minute after minute after minute. Every 60 seconds, without fail.
It then dawned on the team that anything operating with such clockwork required, well, a clock. How else could they explain the uncanny timing?
Searching for clues
To that hypothesis, the researchers started close to home, installing more than 80 smart power quality meters around the Jülich campus. The research site is outfitted with medium- and low-voltage distribution lines, transformers, solar panels, and battery energy storage systems that serve as uninterruptible power supplies (UPS). It also has a high-performance computer system as well as the usual office computers powered by much smaller UPS devices. The power quality meters sampled a range of attributes, including frequency, voltage, current, and power, once every three seconds.
Before long, the research team had its answer. The measurements recorded on the transformer attached to the battery energy storage system peaked every minute, just like on the bigger power grids.
It turns out that many stationary batteries, from data center UPSes to large grid-scale batteries, check their state-of-charge every minute. Since these devices are internet-connected, their clocks are in near perfect synchronicity. Every time one checks its charge, the disturbance is imperceptible on the wide grid. But when they all do it together, that disruption becomes apparent.
To find evidence that UPSes were the main culprit on the grid, Witthaut and his team turned to data provided by grid operators. They found their answer in Ireland.
There, data centers have grown to consume a large fraction of the country’s electricity. By 2022, data centers represented 18% of the load on Ireland’s grid, and each facility is served by a fleet of UPSes. Sure enough, between 2016 and 2021, the minute-by-minute frequency drop on the Irish grid quadrupled from 3 milli-Hertz (mHz) in 2016 to 12 mHz in 2021. More recently, some drops have exceeded 20 mHz.
Ireland’s 50 Hz grid is built to withstand swings of plus or minus 200 mHz, though the grid operator would rather limit the swings to 100 mHz. In that range, 20 mHz isn’t a lot, but data centers aren’t the only loads on the grid. If other loads also cause the frequency to sag, the extra bump from every UPS checking its state-of-charge could push the grid toward blackout conditions.
The solution
The problem is entirely preventable. Rather than check state-of-charge exactly on the minute, Witthaus and team recommend that UPS and grid-scale battery manufacturers add some randomization to the schedule.
While UPSes are driving the problem today, there’s a risk that the phenomenon could persist. The researchers also tested IoT devices. In devices as diverse as a smart oven and Raspberry Pi clusters, they were able to detect periodic power fluctuations. The fix is also a simple software patch, but many IoT devices go unpatched. A recent study found that less than 3% of IoT devices are running the latest firmware.
Regulators may soon have to step in to demand changes, but they can only address their corner of the grid. Given the global nature of the issue, it’ll ultimately require global coordination. The mystery may be solved, but the problem could remain for years to come.

articles.title: Artist Bhagya Ajaikumar explains how good curation balances individual expression and collective vision
articles.text:
Artist Bhagya Ajaikumar explains how good curation balances individual expression and collective vision
In this photo essay, we showcase the ‘Bhoomi’ exhibition at Venkatappa Art Gallery, along with curator insights.
Launched in 2014, PhotoSparks is a weekly feature from YourStory, with photographs that celebrate the spirit of creativity and innovation. In the earlier 1,030 posts, we featured an art festival, cartoon gallery. world music festival, telecom expo, millets fair, climate change expo, wildlife conference, startup festival, Diwali rangoli, and jazz festival.
The Venkatappa and Swasti art galleries in Bengaluru recently hosted the group exhibition titled Bhoomi (see our coverage of earlier exhibitions at Venkatappa gallery here). It was curated by Bhagya Ajaikumar and Pradeep Kumar DM, with works by around 40 artists.
The Swasti gallery was launched in Bengaluru in 2007 to promote art and raise funds for the HCG Foundation as support for cancer patients. Since 2018, Swasti has also conducted art therapy events for cancer patients and their family members.
Dedicated art space in a hospital setting gives a positive energy to patients and their family members. With that goal in mind, Swasti has been actively involved in organising art shows, camps and workshops, with artists coming from across the country and abroad.
“I am currently planning and working on several exciting projects, both as an artist and a curator. This includes a solo presentation titled THANDAV, featuring my art creations inspired by classical Indian dance,” Ajaikumar tells YourStory.
The exhibition will be presented at the RASA cultural festival at Prestige Auditorium in Bengaluru, January 8-10. 2027. She is also curating the upcoming third International KALA Symposium in Mysuru.
“With the vision of art as a catalyst for healing and development, the symposium is conceived as a creative platform connecting fine art, healthcare philanthropy, and grassroots community development. It will be hosted at Bharath Cancer Hospital,” she adds.
Her gallery is also planning an art activity with paediatric oncology patients to celebrate Children's Day this month. “Another ongoing initiative is the installation of artworks in consultation rooms across our hospitals,” Ajaikumar says.
As trends in Indian contemporary art, she points to the revival of traditional Indian art forms through contemporary interpretations. “Styles such as Madhubani, Gond, Pichwai and Mysore are being explored through acrylics on canvas, square compositions, minimalistic presentations, and unconventional materials,” she observes.
“With increasing competition and the pressure to produce work within shorter periods, many traditional processes are gradually disappearing. Traditional knowledge and techniques should also be respected,” she affirms.
Another exciting development is the transformation of traditional Indian crafts into large-scale contemporary installations. “Some traditional art forms are moving beyond small-format works on paper to large canvases, murals and public installations,” she says.
Indian contemporary art is also responding to changes in social, political and environmental realities. “Many artists are exploring themes of identity, migration, displacement, urbanisation, globalisation, and ecology. They encourage viewers to question and reflect on the world around them,” Ajaikumar observes.
“I believe this shift is important because art should not merely be decorative. It can communicate ideas, challenge perceptions and create awareness about issues that affect society,” she affirms.
Collectors are increasingly interested in theme-based series rather than isolated, standalone artworks. “Conceptual works, installations, environmentally conscious practices, and works addressing social and women's issues are receiving greater attention,” she adds.
As for tech trends, AI offers digital artists exciting tools and possibilities for experimentation. “However, use of AI also raises important questions about originality, authorship, authenticity and the value of the human hand and imagination in art,” she cautions.
“Another development I find particularly encouraging is the increasing presence of art in public spaces, especially airports. Major airports in cities such as Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru are providing opportunities to showcase large-scale artworks and installations,” she observes (see our photo essay on art and design at Bengaluru’s airport here).
With their large spaces, airports can bring art closer to people who may not necessarily visit galleries or museums. “These installations often combine art, architecture, unconventional materials, and multimedia practices. They can transform otherwise functional spaces into engaging cultural environments,” she adds.
The exhibitor lineup in her Bhoomi exhibition includes Meenakshi Chinna Rathod, Meghana Gante Ravish, Nagappa Pradhani, Nikhil R Sharma, Nirmala Kumari CS, Premkumar K, Ranganath Amrad, Revanasiddayya SH, Renuka Markande, SG Vasudev, and Santosh Pattar.
Akshay Bhat is an emerging contemporary artist from Karnataka whose practice reflects an interest in expressive visual language and contemporary aesthetics. Alka Chavda is a contemporary visual artist whose practice centres on painting and mixed media.
Renuka Markande is an accomplished artist, educator and researcher whose creative practice bridges academic inquiry and contemporary visual expression. Bhagya Ajaikumar explores expressive painting and the emotional possibilities of colour and form.
Hanumanta T frequently draws inspiration from local traditions, landscapes and everyday human interactions, transforming familiar imagery into evocative narratives. Ishwarayya OM explores themes of identity, environment and human resilience.
Manushya explores universal themes of humanity, coexistence and personal identity through painting and interdisciplinary practice. Marishamachar draws inspiration from regional narratives and lived experience, and creates works that resonate with both cultural specificity and universal human concerns.
As a curator of such a diverse exhibition, Ajaikumar particularly likes placing emerging artists alongside established professionals. “This allows them to learn from one another and gain greater exposure,” she explains.
“I believe that an exhibition should offer more than a collection of individual artworks. It should create a meaningful visual and intellectual experience for the viewer,” she says.
This can be particularly challenging when working with a specific theme. “The curator must establish a meaningful connection between the exhibition's concept and the individual artist's interpretation. There should be a common thread connecting their contributions,” she describes.
“Curators also encourage emerging artists and help them develop their ideas. A carefully curated exhibition can challenge younger artists to think beyond their usual boundaries, experiment with new approaches and raise the quality of their work,” Ajaikumar signs off.
Now what have you done today to pause in your busy schedule and harness your creative side for a better world?
(All photographs taken by Madanmohan Rao on location at Venkatappa Art Gallery.)

articles.title: El cangrejo azul no tenía depredadores naturales en el mediterráneo, hasta que el pulpo empezó a tener hambre
articles.text:
El 2 de octubre de 2022, un buceador fotografió una hembra de cangrejo azul caminando por la arena de San Antoni de Portmany en Ibiza. Le faltaba una pinza y medía 16 centímetros de ancho.
Una hora después, el cangrejo volvió a pasar por el mismo sitio, pero no estaba solo. Un pulpo de unos 850 gramos lo cubría con los brazos. En poco más de 15 minutos, sobre la arena del fondo del mar solo quedaba un trozo del caparazón y la otra pinza.
Puede parecer una curiosidad, pero es mucho más: se trata de uno de los tres primeros registros mediterráneos de un pulpo cazando cangrejos azules adultos en libertad.
¿Qué tiene todo esto de llamativo? Lo interesante no es que un pulpo se coma un cangrejo, sino el tamaño de su presa. Hasta donde sabíamos, el pulpo común suele cazar cangrejos pequeños. De hecho, las presas de más de 10 centímetros de ancho de caparazón son raras incluso para especies de pulpo más grandes y fuertes. Y estos que se han documentado son cangrejos mucho más grandes de 10 cm.
El asunto aquí, se dieron cuenta los investigadores, es que las rarezas no se quedaban ahí: todas las víctimas eran hembras.
¿Y eso? No es evidente, pero la respuesta apareció de repente y es más sencilla de lo que parece. Pulpos y cangrejos no viven a la misma "altura": los segundos viven mucho más abajo que los primeros y solo hay un momento en el que se cruzan: cuando las hembras ascienden para desovar. Ahí es cuando los pulpos las cazan.
Pero, ¿por qué? Es decir, por qué ahora. Si fuera algo 'normal' (y, creedme, las hembras de cangrejo llevan teniendo la mala costumbre de subir para desovar desde hace muchos años) lo deberíamos haber visto antes. Y no lo habíamos visto. Es más, estábamos convencidos de que apenas había depredadores naturales documentados para los cangrejos azules en el Mediterráneo.
Al menos, para cangrejos de ese tamaño. Italia ya había lanzado decenas de miles de crías de pulpo frente a los cangrejos, pero la idea era que se comieran a los pequeños. Esto cambia las cosas.
No obstante, no quiero desviarme. La pregunta clave es por qué ahora y no hay muchas posibilidades: que falta comida.
Un Mediterráneo en llamas. El mar Mediterráneo lleva años encadenando olas de calor récord y eso ha debilitado los ecosistemas de toda la región. Eso es "menos comida" y, por tanto, los pulpos se arriesgan más para encontrar comida.
No tenemos pruebas claras, pero tampoco demasiadas dudas: los pulpos no solo están comiendo, están mandándonos una señal de alerta.

articles.title: Jurista propone que cada respuesta de un chatbot basada en noticias genere un pago a los medios
articles.text:
Un jurista de la Universidad de Ámsterdam propuso que cada respuesta de un chatbot basada en periodismo genere un pago a los medios, como ocurre con los derechos de autor de la música. Lo planteó en una reciente conferencia que la emisora alemana Deutsche Welle (DW) organizó en Berlín.
Martin Senftleben, director del Instituto de Derecho de la Información de esa universidad, distingue dos usos del periodismo: el entrenamiento de los modelos y las respuestas a preguntas concretas. Dijo que el pago por entrenamiento es una cuestión legal más compleja. Lo urgente, sostuvo, es el uso de noticias para responder en tiempo real.
Su idea es un sistema de pago obligatorio por ley. Una entidad recaudadora juntaría el dinero y lo repartiría entre editores y periodistas, igual que las sociedades de gestión de derechos musicales. Con esas tarifas como referencia, los medios podrían negociar luego acuerdos individuales con las empresas de IA.
Senftleben sostuvo que el derecho europeo vigente ya permitiría reclamos colectivos de pago, sin esperar una nueva ley. “¿A qué estamos esperando? Alemania es un Estado miembro grande. Esto debería introducirse en Alemania”, dijo ante los asistentes.
Medios que ven menos tráfico y menos dinero
Julia Becker, editora del grupo de medios alemán Funke, dijo que antes los buscadores indexaban los sitios y enviaban lectores a cambio, y que “ese intercambio se rompió”. Pidió una compensación justa por el uso de contenidos, impuestos para las tecnológicas y reglas claras para la IA.
La directora general de DW, Barbara Massing, afirmó que las empresas de IA usan el reportaje de calidad para generar respuestas, pero que ese trabajo queda “en gran parte invisible” al final del proceso. Pidió que las fuentes periodísticas aparezcan identificadas y enlazadas en las respuestas de los chatbots.
Según una encuesta de 2026 del Instituto Reuters para el Estudio del Periodismo, con más de 90.000 personas en el mundo, el 10% usa chatbots para informarse cada semana. La cifra es mayor entre los jóvenes, según DW, que cita ese estudio.
En octubre, las emisoras alemanas ARD y RTL y dos asociaciones de editores pidieron reforzar los derechos de autor de los medios. En Estados Unidos, The New York Times demandó a Brave Software por usar sus contenidos sin permiso y evitar su muro de pago, según DW.
Google ofrece negociar, otro experto advierte sobre más reglas
Lutz Mache, gerente de asuntos públicos de Google, dijo en el panel que la empresa está dispuesta a negociar acuerdos con los medios alemanes. Señaló que sus pagos por derechos conexos de prensa cubren a más de 800 publicaciones de Alemania, según la versión en inglés de DW.
Google prueba además un piloto llamado “AI Contribution” con editores seleccionados, que busca recompensar el contenido que pesa de forma significativa en las respuestas de Gemini y de los resúmenes de IA del buscador. DW aclara que es un experimento inicial y no un sistema de pago abierto a todos los editores.
Jörg Heidrich, abogado de tecnología y comisionado de IA del grupo alemán Heise, advirtió contra sumar reglas sin medir sus efectos. Dijo que Europa ya quedó rezagada en la carrera de la IA y que nuevas restricciones podrían perjudicar a startups, desarrolladores independientes e instituciones de investigación que necesitan datos para entrenar sistemas.
Audiencias eligen fuentes de información digitales, incluyendo chatbots de IA
Según el Informe sobre Noticias Digitales 2025 del Instituto Reuters de la Universidad de Oxford, que encuestó a 12.149 personas en Argentina, Brasil, Chile, Colombia, México y Perú, el consumo de noticias en América Latina se desplaza cada vez más hacia plataformas digitales, incluidos los chatbots de inteligencia artificial como ChatGPT y Claude, que pasaron de un 6% a un 10% de usuarios en un año, mientras cae levemente el acceso por televisión y diarios impresos.
Sin embargo, este desplazamiento convive con una caída de la confianza en las noticias, que bajó al 31% en la región, el nivel más bajo a nivel global, con Brasil como el país más confiado (36%) y Argentina y Colombia entre los más desconfiados (26% y 25%).

articles.title: Sequoia partners reportedly blindsided when Roelof Botha joined SpaceX board | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Sequoia Capital announced some major changes this week, including the closure of its London office, the merger of its early-stage and growth teams, and the end of its Scouts program.
Now, the Financial Times has published a report painting all of this as an attempt to undo the legacy of former leader Roelof Botha, who stepped down as the firm’s steward last year. An unnamed source told the FT that Botha “loved process and hierarchy,” while “the rest of the team didn’t.”
Apparently, not everyone is on-board with the changes, with another source firing back that this seems like an “erasure of Sequoia’s heritage, not Roelof’s legacy.”
The break between Botha and his old firm reportedly deepened after Botha joined the SpaceX board this summer. (Botha and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk previously worked together at PayPal.) A source told the FT that Sequoia’s partners were blindsided by the announcement, because Botha “didn’t ask compliance, he didn’t get sign off from the partnership” — even though his new role could complicate the firm’s ability to trade its $20 billion stake.
A Sequoia spokesperson said that the firm continues to “collaborate closely” with Botha.

articles.title: Physicists listened to electrical noise to crack a superconductor mystery
articles.text:
Superconductors carry electricity without resistance, but most only work a few degrees above absolute zero. In the late 1980s, copper-based materials called cuprates were found to superconduct at higher temperatures—reachable with affordable liquid nitrogen. Yet nearly 40 years later, physicists still don’t agree on why.
In a recent Science study, a team of physicists led by Milan Allan of Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich and Ingmar Swart of Utrecht University in the Netherlands has found some answers by listening to the faint electrical crackle of current flowing into a cuprate.
The missing electrons
Central to the mystery of cuprates’ high-temperature superconductivity is a strange state called the pseudogap. “The pseudogap is a phenomenon of missing electrons,” Allan said. Above the temperature at which cuprates become superconducting, some of their electrons seem to vanish—measurements find far fewer of them at the energies where they should be. “Everybody knows that from different probes, you see that there’s these vanishing electrons, but nobody knows why,” Allan said.
Over the decades, physicists have put forward two main competing explanations. The first hypothesizes that the electrons get stuck in some sort of structure. In this view, electrons freeze into patterns, such as charge density waves, and superconductivity develops separately. The alternative explanation tightly links this phenomenon to superconductivity. “Other people think they’re missing because they form pairs,” Allan said. Pairs of electrons, called Cooper pairs, are what carry current in a superconductor. If, as the material cools, these pairs appear before the material becomes superconducting, they would be a precondition of superconductivity, a waiting room of sorts, where pairs exist but can’t yet move together in lockstep.
Settling this proved extremely hard. “Lots of different experimental signatures are kind of lumped inside this,” Allan said. Different instruments all see something, but their readings, Allan said, are never conclusive. “It’s always something kind of incoherent, hard to grasp,” he said. What the researchers needed was a way to see pairs directly, and Allan and his colleagues figured it out.

articles.title: Just a moonshot? Google energy head claims data centers in space would cost up to 100x more than on Earth
articles.text:
Just a moonshot? Google energy head claims data centers in space would cost up to 100x more than on Earth
Space data centers could be a costly choice, Google warns
- Google global head of data center energy says space data centers could cost up to 100 times more than terrestrial ones
- Amanda Peterson Corio's remarks came weeks after Google launched its first Suncatcher prototype, a roughly 1kW satellite that has since run Gemma 4 on an orbiting TPU, one chip at a time
- Corio says the real bottleneck on Earth is permitting rather than power, the same politics that backers of orbital compute claim they can escape
Google has spent the past month showing off AI chips working in orbit, but the executive responsible for powering its data centers back on Earth has just put a sobering price on the idea.
Speaking at The Information's recent WTF Summit in Napa Valley, Amanda Peterson Corio, Google's global head of data center energy, said data centers in space could cost up to 100 times as much as those built on the ground.
Her advice to the rest of the industry was simple and (pun intended) grounded: "Let's explore all the terrestrial options before we go extraterrestrial."
A very expensive proposition?
The remarks land at an awkward moment, because Google is testing exactly this kind of hardware right now. Its first Project Suncatcher prototype, built with satellite operator Planet, launched on SpaceX's Transporter-18 rideshare mission on October 1.
Google recently also announced its Hello World milestone: an onboard Gemma 4 model, running on a TPU, wrote a short haiku about being in space, which was downlinked as the satellite passed over Svalbard, Norway.
The company bills this as the first AI response from a data center-class TPU in orbit. That is a carefully measured claim, given that Starcloud put an Nvidia H100 into orbit a year ago and was running AI models on it within weeks.
Scale is the bigger caveat and one that can be easily overlooked amidst the hype: The satellite carries four TPUs but generates only about 1kW of solar power, so it can run just one chip at a time for roughly 20 minutes per session, according to The Next Web. A single 1 GW AI campus, the kind now under construction on the ground, draws about a million times that much power.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Google has described Suncatcher as a "moonshot" since it was unveiled a year ago, and project lead Travis Beals told NPR on launch day that he did not expect orbital compute to become cheaper than the terrestrial kind within the next five years.
Not the first or last skeptic of orbital datacenters
This did start a somewhat interesting conversation on Wall Street; Short seller Jim Chanos read Corio's statement as $5 trillion per gigawatt of compute, and posted on X that the gap between her view and the estimates of SpaceX management and bulls "should give pause to anyone trying to model this business out."
TIKR pushed the arithmetic further by examining recent claims: SpaceX's CFO told investors last month that new compute pays for itself in under a year at current rental rates. Built in orbit at up to 100 times the cost and rented at the same price, TIKR calculated that payback stretches to as long as a century, or about a decade even at a tenth of Corio's stated ceiling.
That matters because orbital compute underpins part of SpaceX's roughly $1.8 trillion market value at the time of writing. The company has asked the FCC for permission to launch up to a million data-center satellites, and Musk has posted that the orbital compute SpaceX deploys each month will probably overtake terrestrial compute around the end of 2028. Yet SpaceX's own IPO paperwork warned investors of "significant technical complexity and unproven technologies," and said its orbital data centers might never become commercially viable.
Corio is hardly the first skeptic. OpenAI's Sam Altman called the idea "ridiculous" under current conditions earlier this year, even as Nvidia lined up a Space-1 Vera Rubin module aimed squarely at orbital data centers.
This is an extremely interesting take from Google's end. Alphabet is one of SpaceX's largest outside shareholders, with a stake disclosed at 6.11% at the end of 2025, according to Bloomberg, and Google has reportedly been in talks with SpaceX about launching future Suncatcher hardware. Its energy chief has questioned and potentially poured cold water on a thesis that props up part of an asset Alphabet owns, while Google's own moonshot depends on cheap SpaceX launches arriving on schedule.
Corio's broader argument, somewhat ironically, was about the ground rather than the sky. According to The Information, she said the US has enough power and that the real bottlenecks are permitting and grid interconnection studies.
She blamed much of the local backlash against data centers on newer, less experienced developers, without naming any, and said Google prepays for grid upgrades over 15 to 20 years in more than 9 states, posts restoration bonds, and has stopped using nondisclosure agreements with local governments.
There is, however, a problem with this argument: Established firms such as Oracle have also faced local resistance, which complicates the idea that inexperienced newcomers are the problem. The backlash is anything but marginal: opposition has spread across the US, and Data Center Watch counted 75 projects worth about $130 billion delayed or blocked in the first quarter of 2026 alone.
There is a political angle built around these arguments that keeps orbital data centers in play, and SpaceX is essentially building on that promise. After this week's midterm elections, in which data center construction was a campaign issue in several races, including the contest for Texas governor, Musk posted, "Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now."
Leaving the planet does not, however, mean leaving the permit queue; SpaceX's million-satellite request and Blue Origin's 51,600-satellite Project Sunrise both need FCC approval, and debris and spectrum concerns give regulators and rivals plenty to object to, just at a higher altitude. If power really is plentiful and permission is the bottleneck, as Corio argues, then orbit's main selling point is jumping that queue, and by her numbers it is a very expensive way to do it.
For now, until someone flies more than a kilowatt-scale test bed and publishes what it actually costs, the multiple between orbit and the ground, whether it turns out to be 3x, 10x, or as much as 100x, remains an educated guess. Corio's stated ceiling is arguably as unproven as Musk's timetable. Only one of those numbers, however, is already priced in considerably into a stock's current valuation, and SpaceX investors will be waiting for financials to back its CEO's claims with bated breath to say the least.

articles.title: Ce qui se passe vraiment sous la coque de votre smartphone quand vous le posez sur un chargeur sans fil
articles.text:
Recharge sans fil : comment fonctionne la charge à induction sur votre smartphone ?
Poser son smartphone sur un simple socle suffit désormais à remplir sa batterie sans fil. Derrière cette petite prouesse du quotidien se cache un phénomène physique vieux de plus de deux siècles.
Recharger son smartphone par câble appartient au passé depuis la démocratisation de la recharge sans fil. Qu’il s’agisse d’un simple chargeur au format galet ou d’un support aimanté, il suffit aujourd’hui d’y déposer son appareil pour récupérer de précieux pourcentages de batterie. Un transfert d’énergie qui interroge, mais qui n’a en réalité rien de bien magique puisqu’il repose sur une loi physique très simple.
Deux bobines de cuivre qui dialoguent grâce au magnétisme
Faire circuler de l’électricité pure directement à l’air libre serait non seulement inefficace, mais surtout très dangereux. Pour contourner l’absence de câble, les chargeurs sans fil répondant aux normes Qi utilisent le principe de l’induction électromagnétique. Le secret repose sur deux bobines de fil de cuivre enroulées à plat : la première est logée dans le support de charge branché au secteur, et la seconde se cache sous le dos de votre smartphone.
Lorsque le courant électrique traverse la bobine du chargeur, il ne cherche pas à sauter vers le téléphone, mais génère plutôt un champ magnétique oscillant juste au-dessus de la base. Dès que vous posez votre mobile dessus, ce champ invisible traverse le verre ou le plastique de la coque et vient agiter les électrons présents dans la bobine réceptrice de l’appareil.
Un phénomène qui donne alors naissance à un nouveau courant électrique directement au cœur de votre téléphone.
La reconversion en courant électrique et le défi de la chaleur
Une fois captée par la bobine interne du smartphone, cette énergie magnétique reprend sa forme initiale. Un petit composant électronique convertit ce courant alternatif induit (créé à distance par le champ magnétique) en courant continu, prêt à être stocké chimiquement dans les cellules lithium-ion de la batterie.
Ce transfert à travers quelques millimètres d’air comporte toutefois une limite physique incontournable : la déperdition d’énergie sous forme de chaleur. Contrairement à un câble qui guide les électrons sans fuite, le champ magnétique se disperse au moindre décalage entre les deux bobines, ce qui ralentit la charge tout en faisant chauffer le dos de l’appareil.
C’est précisément pour aligner parfaitement ces deux anneaux de cuivre et limiter la chauffe qu’Apple, suivi par la norme Qi2 sur Android, a intégré une couronne d’aimants autour du système de charge avec la technologie MagSafe (Pixelsnap sur les Google Pixel).

articles.title: 120€ de moins qu'à sa sortie : ce casque Sony profite du 11.11 d'AliExpress
articles.text:
Noté 9/10 par notre rédaction, le casque antibruit de Sony profite du 11.11 d’AliExpress pour repasser nettement sous son prix de lancement, à trois semaines du Black Friday. Le WH-1000XM6 s’affiche à 329,48 € avec le code CLU60, soit 120 € de moins qu’à sa sortie, même si nous l’avions déjà vu plus bas en septembre.
Sorti en mai 2025 à 450 €, le Sony WH-1000XM6 a succédé au WH-1000XM5 en corrigeant presque tous ses défauts, au point de décrocher 9/10 dans notre test. Pour le 11.11, AliExpress le propose à 329,48 € au lieu de 408 € dans son coloris Platinum Silver, à condition de saisir le code CLU60 au moment de payer.
La remise atteint 78,52 €, soit environ 19 %, et l’écart dépasse 120 € par rapport au prix de lancement. C’est un bon niveau de prix, pas un record : nous l’avions déjà relayé à 256,05 € chez AliExpress en septembre. L’offre vise d’abord celles et ceux qui passent des heures dans les transports ou en open space et veulent couper le bruit.
Pour le 11.11, le Sony WH-1000XM6 Platinum Silver passe à 329,48 € au lieu de 408 € sur AliExpress, avec le code CLU60 à saisir au paiement.
Pourquoi choisir le Sony WH-1000XM6 ?
- Le silence sur commande : La puce QN3 pilote 12 microphones, six de chaque côté, et notre test constate que les bruits sourds de moteur disparaissent presque totalement. Même les voix, plus difficiles à atténuer, sont nettement filtrées.
- Un confort enfin à la hauteur : Sony a élargi l’arceau et épaissi les coussinets, deux points reprochés au XM5. Le casque de 254 g s’est montré très confortable dans notre test, y compris sur de longues sessions.
- De l’endurance et de la souplesse : Nous avons mesuré environ 32 heures d’autonomie avec la réduction de bruit active, et 3 minutes de charge rendent 3 heures d’écoute. Le multipoint permet de garder le casque connecté au PC et au smartphone en même temps.
Du train au bureau, un casque qui sait se faire oublier
Dans le train, en avion ou en open space, c’est l’isolation qui justifie l’achat. Dans notre test du Sony WH-1000XM6, nous l’avons jugée exemplaire, tout comme le mode transparence, très naturel quand il faut entendre une annonce ou un collègue. Côté son, la signature reste généreuse dans le grave, mais elle déborde moins sur les voix que sur le XM5, ce qui rend musique et podcasts plus lisibles.
Le profil type est celui du navetteur, du voyageur fréquent ou du télétravailleur qui enchaîne les visioconférences : les 12 micros servent aussi aux appels, très clairs dans un environnement calme. Le constat est moins flatteur dans un vacarme extrême, où le kit mains libres montre ses limites. Si vous comptez brancher le casque en filaire sans l’allumer, le rendu en mode passif vous décevra, et l’absence de mode USB Audio ferme la porte à l’écoute par câble USB-C. Enfin, si vous écoutez surtout au calme chez vous, cette réduction de bruit perd beaucoup de son intérêt.
Face à Apple et Bose, ce que ce Sony apporte vraiment
Le WH-1000XM6 joue la carte de la technologie plutôt que celle du luxe : il est entièrement en plastique, là où l’AirPods Max 2, que notre classement réserve plutôt aux possesseurs d’iPhone, coûte nettement plus cher. Le Bose QuietComfort Ultra reste devant sur le confort selon notre test, quand le Sony mise sur une connectivité très complète, LDAC, LE Audio et multipoint compris. Notre comparatif des meilleurs casques Bluetooth le présente comme le modèle le plus technologique de sa sélection, aux côtés d’options bien plus abordables comme le Nothing Headphone (a), qui occupe la tête du classement.
✅ Les points forts
- Réduction de bruit et mode transparence jugés exemplaires dans notre test
- Confort revu grâce à l’arceau élargi et aux coussinets épaissis
- Environ 32 heures d’autonomie mesurées avec la réduction de bruit
- LDAC, LE Audio (LC3) et connexion multipoint
- Casque de nouveau pliable, livré avec une housse rigide magnétique
❌ Les limites
- Conception tout plastique, à la surface assez salissante
- Rendu décevant en mode filaire passif, et pas de mode USB Audio
- Appels moins clairs dans un environnement très bruyant
- Prix déjà vu plus bas chez AliExpress en septembre, à 256,05 €
Le prix de 329,48 € dépend du code CLU60 : vérifiez qu’il apparaît bien dans votre panier AliExpress avant de régler votre Sony WH-1000XM6.
À 329,48 €, le Sony WH-1000XM6 redevient un achat raisonnable pour un casque noté 9/10, dont l’isolation, le confort et l’autonomie collent aux longues journées casque sur les oreilles. Navetteurs, voyageurs fréquents et télétravailleurs en open space en profiteront le plus. Le gain est réel face au prix de lancement, mais l’offre ne bat pas les 256,05 € que nous avions relayés en septembre.
Si vous visez à tout prix le tarif plancher, le Black Friday peut encore faire bouger les prix, sans aucune garantie. Si vous vivez dans l’écosystème Apple, l’AirPods Max 2 s’intégrera mieux à vos appareils, pour bien plus cher. Pour tous les autres, le 11.11 offre l’occasion de passer à un casque qui fait réellement taire l’environnement, sans payer le prix fort de sa sortie.

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admits to having an affair with suspected Chinese spy — Jensen apologizes in letter to staff, company board forms independent committee to investigate
articles.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admits to an affair with a suspected Chinese spy — Jensen apologizes in letter to staff, company board forms independent committee to investigate
CEO admits to adultery.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair with a woman who is allegedly a Chinese spy. His apology came in a letter to Nvidia staff, which you can read in full below. Nvidia's board of directors released a statement late on Sunday to address the bombshell report that U.S. intelligence believes Huang had an affair with a Chinese spy. The board says it has no reason to believe sensitive corporate information or U.S. national security was compromised, but the company intends to examine all available information to determine what happened.
The BoD claims it is fully confident in Jensen Huang and his leadership team. Huang, who has been married to his wife, Lori Huang, for 41 years, says he fully supports the investigation.
"A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation," a statement by Nvidia's BoD reads. "The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of Nvidia and its shareholders. […] Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it."
On Friday, the first reporting emerged claiming U.S. intelligence agencies believe Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who was allegedly recruited by China's Ministry of State Security (MSS) to gather information and help Chinese companies obtain restricted AI GPUs. The company has been on the radar for smuggling restricted hardware to China since at least 2025: Megaspeed has been accused of smuggling $2 billion worth of AI chips into China via its subsidiary Speedmatrix.
Nvidia has strenuously rejected suggestions of improper dealings, saying that its CEO regularly meets thousands of customers and that these interactions do not involve sensitive corporate information or national security secrets. Chinese officials have also dismissed the espionage allegations as unfounded.
The suspected Chinese intelligence operation targeting Jensen has not been independently confirmed as a fact. The relationship is alleged to follow the typical "honeypot" strategy, wherein foreign intelligence agencies use operatives to ensnare targets into romantic relationships to steal information and influence their decision-making.
Huang has been an outspoken critic of those opposed to limiting the supply of AI GPUs to China. Huang recently expressed his opinion that the label 'China hawk' is not a badge of honor Americans should wear; it is really 'a badge of shame.' Huang also said it "doesn’t have to be all us or them. It could be us and them," drawing fire from others in the administration and other tech companies, including the CEO of Palantir.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
"I owe my family and all of you an apology," Huang wrote. "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry. Throughout my life, my family has given me love and support. They deserve my honesty and loyalty. Instead, I let them down and damaged the life we built together. I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it. To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust."
In June 2018, Intel chief executive Brian Krzanich resigned after an internal investigation, assisted by external legal counsel, confirmed that he had engaged in a consensual romantic relationship with an Intel employee, which violated the company's non-fraternization policy applicable to all managers. Krzanich, who had led Intel since 2013, also stepped down from the company's board, while then-chief financial officer Robert Swan took over as interim CEO. For now, it remains unclear if Jensen will meet a similar fate and lose control of the company he founded.
Jensen's full letter to staff reads as follows:
To my colleagues at NVIDIA, I owe my family and all of you an apology. I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry. 
Throughout my life, my family has given me love and support. They deserve my honesty and loyalty. Instead, I let them down and damaged the life we built together. I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it.
To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust.
To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me. Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence.
Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, NVIDIA’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American.
My family bears no responsibility for my choices. I do. Please give them privacy.
Jensen
The whole statement from Nvidia's Board of Directors reads as follows:
The Nvidia Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.
A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation.
The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders.
While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information.
Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it.
The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.

Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.
